117790:
You dock at a small, lively port on the northern coast. While most of your crew replenish supplies and repair the damage suffered in a recent storm, some decide to head off to explore the local souq.

Streets fold and unfold into each other, bedecked in a wild array of colours and dizzyingly heady unknown scents, which so confuse your sailors that they become lost in the weave of passages. Seeing their distress, several young men in beggarly clothes offer to guide them through the maze.
117792: Shoo them off and trust your crew’s instincts.
117793:
It takes some observation, but your sailors soon understand that the mosaic of low-hanging cloths are arranged in specific patterns. A sharp right after a spice dealer’s enthusiastic attempt to sell your crew a few years’ worth of ochre and red powders leads them to a small, shadowed plaza, where two musicians are strumming many-stringed zithers of rich-honeyed wood.
There is a peacefulness to this place that soothes your crew, and they try to engage the musicians in conversation to learn more about their culture.
117794: Attempt to hail them in their native tongue.
117795:
Your crew’s linguistic efforts attract much appreciative surprise, and a lively conversation soon sparks up, supplemented by voluminous approximative sign language and much laughter.
Before your sailors can object, an intricate tea set is brought out, and the small pewter cups are soon brimming with steaming, crisp-scented mint tea, supplemented by flavoursome pastries. Many tales are traded, and nightfall has long since passed when your crew return to the ship, arms laden with simple but intricate tokens of friendship.
117796: Your crew barely knows enough of the language to greet the locals, let alone carry their questions. After a few long minutes of polite puzzlement, they courteously but pointedly turn away. Frustrated, your crew retreat to the ship, hoping the next port encountered will be slightly more cosmopolitan.
117797: Gesticulate to try and convey your meaning.
117798: Not wishing to interrupt the music, one sailor walks up to a man about to enter a nearby house and taps his shoulder to attract his attention. The man turns a curious face to this unexpected intervention.
117799: Gesture between your mouth and the man, indicating you wish to speak to him.
117800: The man’s face darkens with anger. He barks a few clearly offensive words and strides across the threshold, slamming the door in your crew’s baffled faces. Judging by the condemning stares they now attract, your sailors understand the gesture they made is considered a great insult, and wisely decide to retreat to the ship before committing another faux pas.
117801: Point out the surroundings and give a thumbs up, indicating you find his home beautiful.
117802: The man starts unpleasantly, visibly insulted, before casting a witheringly contemptuous glare at your expectant crew. Judging by the condemning stares they are suddenly attracting, your sailors understand the gesture must have some unknown, possibly derogatory meaning here, and wisely decide to retreat to the ship before committing another faux pas.
117803: Place your hand on your heart to indicate you are glad to meet him.
117804:
The man smiles, and a conversation slowly begins, accompanied by a smattering of local idioms and considerable use of sign language. Understanding your crew to be foreign, he promptly invites them in and welcomes them with generous helpings of piping mint tea and soft, honeyed pastries.
When your crew part ways with him, they cannot help but feel comfort in the knowledge such friendships, beyond words and shared history, may still be found.
117805:
It is not long before your crew are hopelessly lost in the tangle of crowded streets. From all parts, merchants assail them with hopeful voices, flaunting the quality of their wares and the attractiveness of their prices in such a way that the sailors soon feel like a sloop buffeted by harsh winds.
One particularly bold and smiling merchant walks up to the lead sailor.
‘I have just the thing for you — rare items, impossible to find elsewhere!’
His wares seem common enough, but perhaps he can give you directions?
117806: Tahanina! You have an eye for fine items!
117807:
The tradeoff hardly seems fair, but your sailors are eager to find a way out of the souq. Once the deal is concluded, the grinning merchant points them to a low set of arched doors nearby that will lead them back to the safety of the harbour.
Your crew try to convince themselves, loudly and unconvincingly, that the bauble will at least make for a decent souvenir, despite its hefty cost.
117808:
You try to haggle the prices down to something reasonable, but it becomes increasingly clear that the merchant has little intention of making an honest deal. This suspicion is confirmed when, after a particularly vehement refusal to pay a fortune for what looks like common kitchenware, he barks a few short words.
Immediately, several burly individuals appear through the draperies at the back of the shop. With a chill, you realise the price to pay has just increased steeply!
117810:
The merchant can barely hide his glee as you hand over the outrageous fee he has just extorted from you. He waves a sardonic goodbye, as his acolytes lead your crew back through the crowded souq to the docks.
Once back aboard the ship, it becomes very tempting to throw the thing overboard, but the officers insist it be kept, tacking a note to it reading ‘Now you know why shore leave is restricted.’
117811: Despite their valiant efforts, your men are severely trounced, and can barely make it back to the ship with their battered comrades before the whole town turns on them.
117813:
Outnumbered though they may be, your sailors settle in for a fight, some of them drawing ribbing knives and various crude but wickedly-edged items from the pockets of their breeches. The thugs' faces fall, discountenanced by these weapons — evidently, they were not prepared for so hostile a reaction, and so safely back a few paces away, behind the dais.
Furious at his men’s cowardice, the merchant has no choice but to mumble directions to the harbour, leaving your crew to operate a swift retreat.
117814: The battle that ensues is brief and bloody. Your men fight as valiantly as they can, but are swiftly overrun and turned out into the street, penniless and bloodied, where they regroup pitifully and hobble back to the ship as precipitously as they can.
117816:
Not one to be so easily shaken off, the merchant steps into your crew’s footsteps, accusingly asking them if they are aware of how rude it is to ignore someone in such a fashion.
The ship’s boy rounds on him angrily.
‘Stop bein’ a bloody pain and scram!’
The man’s expression sours, and he steps forward and grabs the lad by the collar. Before anyone can react, your crew realize the altercation has attracted a crowd of hostile locals, some of them reaching for long knives.
117817: Seize the merchant and use him as a shield.
117818:
One of your topmen leaps forward, twisting the merchant’s arm violently before pulling him in front to use as a shield.
There's a moment’s bated silence as the surrounding cut-throats hesitate, before rushing forward with a roar of outrage.
Outnumbered but well-versed in close-quarters combat, your crew throw the merchant into the charge, scattering the assailants, and promptly disarm and subdue their leaders.
Cowed and bruised, the thugs slink back to side streets, as your crew operate a hasty retreat to the safety of the ship.
117819: Fearing for their lives, your crew have no choice but to flee to the ship, leaving the lad to bleed out on the dusty street.
117820: Pay him. No amount of money is worth the lives of your crew.
117821:
Fearing the result of a confrontation, the sailors fumble for some money, handing out various coins and valuables to the expectant merchant.
A quick command, and the ill-gotten treasure disappears into a worn-leather purse around the merchant’s neck. The man smirks, fingering his dagger ominously – much to the merriment of his henchmen.
Unwilling to tarry any longer, your crew turn heels and flee the scene, cheeks burning with the trailing sound of scornful hilarity.
117822: Fearing for their lives, your crew have no choice but to flee to the ship, leaving the lad to bleed out on the dusty street.
117823: Ignore his banter and ask him for directions.
117824:
Ignoring the outstretched wares, one of your sailors uses what little she knows of the local language to ask the man for the quickest path to the harbour.
He flounders, evidently conflicted, before mumbling a series of nigh-incomprehensible directions.
Your crew follow them as best they can, but whether due to their cryptic nature, or to your sailors’ general ineptitude in terms of orientation, it takes them the better part of the afternoon to find a way out of the souq and back onto the ship.
117825: Examine the ragged men to find a suitable guide.
117826:
One of your crew members singles out a promising intellectual, with sleeves intricately patterned with dark arabesque lines. It is only when he eagerly draws nearer that you realise the lines are actually inked directly upon his skin — the verses of holy texts in his native script.

It is evident that he is well-learned despite his lowly means, and so helpful is he in describing the lore and history of the city that your diplomat cannot help but be impressed by his earnestness. When the time comes to pay him, your sailor instead offers him an apprenticeship, with your captain’s approval.The young man, however, is reticent, and claims his elderly family could not provide for itself without him.
117827: Insist upon meeting his family in the hope of convincing them
117828:
The man’s home is barely more than a hovel, tucked away in an alcove on one of the narrower kuchehs threading the souq. His parents greet you worried, offering bland tea with oft-infused leaves, and it pains you to think it is probably the best they have to offer.
The debate is long and heated, with much arguing back and forth: the elderly couple are evidently worried as to their fate when they can no longer provide for themselves. However it is with a heavy heart that they ultimately relent and give him their blessing, imploring you to care for him as one of your own.
117829:
You follow the young man to a small, crowded room in one of the riads overlooking the market, where an aged couple greet you tersely. Their mood darkens as soon as they understand that you are asking to take their son away, and they firmly turn down your many arguments and offers.
‘The Book says the young must support the aged in the dusk of their life. Who are you to deny this?’ You think to reply that their son is no spring chicken himself, but
sensing their resolve, you have no choice but to relent and bid him a disappointed farewell.
117830: Insist: such talent should not be wasted.
117831:
Flattered at first, the man soon wearies of your insistence.
‘I have duties here, and a family to care for. Your offer does you credit, but what are promises made by strangers newly met, however honourable, in the eyes of the duty imparted by the Almighty? My place is here.’
His tone as he finishes giving you a tour of the city is cooler, but when you part ways, he smiles, and you reward him generously for his expertise.
117832: Respect his conviction and sense of duty.
117833:
No man should feel compelled to loftier destinies if their duty calls them elsewhere. Your crew compliment him on his sense of loyalty to his kin, and tip him handsomely for his guidance and company.
By way of a parting gift, he traces a few elegant lines on a small piece of paper — an errant verse from a poem he is working on — before disappearing back into the souq.
Roughly translated, the line reads ‘Mine was a life divinely ordained, and thus I knew serenity’, and is signed with the lad’s name, Qaddr Razzaq.
117834:
The men throng around you in a clamour of self-professed learnedness and helpfulness. Overwhelmed, you select a young man whose confidence and insistence seem to make him a wise option.
It is soon painfully obvious, however, that he was a poor choice. Though he does take you through the colourful and bustling souq, he has little to say about it, and his pace is brisk.
After an hour of so, you reach a remote and secluded part of the market, only to have him turn to you sombrely, declaring his guided tour complete and demanding an extortionate fee for his services.
117835: Grit your teeth and pay the fee.
117836: Even a blatantly extortionate scheme such as this is better than risking being trapped in such an isolated part of town. Reluctantly, you hand over the hefty sum, and he deftly pockets it before disappearing into a nearby alley, leaving your crew to find their own way back to the ship — only now with lighter purses, and much animosity towards the locals.
117837: Visibly upset at being denied his due, the young man starts chattering angrily in his native tongue. Your crew attempt to leave the place and find their own way back to the harbour through the stench of nearby tanneries, but your guide follows your every footstep, insisting upon being paid in increasingly loud and aggressive tones. You attempt to ignore him, but his relentlessness is sorely testing your crew's patience.
117838: Attempt to intimidate and scare him away.
117839:
One of your sailors lashes out angrily at the young man, cuffing him sharply behind the head. ‘Learn your place, boy!’
He staggers slightly, dazed and shocked, terror welling up in his gaze. Before anyone can step in, he ducks behind a great vat of bubbling dyes and flees your sailors’ wrath.
While navigating a path back to the harbour, your crew cannot help but feel guilty at their treatment of the boy — when one is so abjectly destitute, it is little surprise that propriety should bow to need.
117840:
One of your sailors steps threateningly towards the boy, reaching out to grab him by the front of his ragged shirt. The lad, however, darts nimbly out of reach, colliding with another surprised sailor before leaping behind a high stratified stack of drying tea leaves. When your men round it, much to the protest of the labourers tending the stack, the lad has disappeared.
As your crew uncertainly head back to the harbour, the man the boy had run into cries out: his belt pouch is missing, evidently stolen!
117841: The lad clearly needs to be taught the error of his ways.
117842:
‘It is natural that securing your basic needs should take precedence over your absolute moral being. But there are resources in the province of lawfulness that you could abide by...' and so on and so forth.
Your sailor’s benevolent, albeit pompous tones have some tempering effect on the lad, but when the lecture is over, you cannot help but wonder how much of it he understood, yet alone took to heart.
117843:
‘Never is there cause to be immoral, lest the principle of morality be neutered. If society is to be society and justice to be justice, there can be no legitimate unlawfulness, and consequently, you must reflect on your immorality and change your ways.’
The young man’s face darkens with every self-important word, and he swiftly turns heel on your sailor, stranding him mid-speech.
As your crew return to the ship, a series of angry mutterings arise from all parts, and a hail of broken earthenware rains down from high windows.
Your crew suffer numerous cuts and bruises.
117854: Try to secure his help by purchasing something.
117855: How pleasant to deal with reasonable people!
117857: Surely you were not expecting my services to be free?
117867:
The lights of Olispo glimmer through the spray as your sailors hasten to secure their mooring. Music and merriment spill from the narrow streets, wafting aromas of warm bread and savoury fish fresh from the tide.
With a thrill of pent up anticipation, the sailors stream off the ship and excitedly crowd onto a pristinely new yellow tram, laughing as it rickets off into the warm night, hailed loudly by festive locals.
A flurry of ample sleeves turns to them genially:
'Boa noite, friends! From whence does the tide bring you?'
117869:
‘Maravilhoso! I have kin there — wonderful people, and hardworking to a fault!
Come, we must drink — and I know just the place. Follow me!’
The sailors clamber off the tram gracelessly, unaccustomed to its peculiar rhythm, before following the man through a maze of passages lit by antique oil lamps hanging from balconies. Stopping before a low stone arch, he reaches through the overgrown ivy, pulling open an unseen door.
A flare of chattering and low lights greets you, wafting dark-scented spirits and fresh-roasted food.‘Try the pasteis de nata, our sweet, secret custardy pride! And of course, our famous port!'
117872: Order a generous round of port and custard pies
117873:
The innkeeper navigates the thronged room expertly, avoiding boisterous patrons to set a large platter onto the table. Your crew swiftly attack the warm pastries, wolfing down the soft custard with aplomb, while Jose introduces a merry waltz of friends, each eager to toast the newcomers to their city.
When the festivities peter out in the late hours of the night, your sailors trickle back the ship, full-bellied, light-headed and free of care.
117874:
The innkeeper scoffs when your crew remark on the price.
‘This is no mere city, amigos. This is Olispo, land of riches and flavour! Surely you do not expect to feast for free!’
There's a minute of long, awkward silence before Jose, obviously crestfallen, clears his throat. Clearly, he had hoped his helpfulness would earn him a night of free food and drink.
With a curt bow and a ‘Boa noite’, he steps out into the night.
Suddenly the crowd seems much less amicable, and you cannot help but wonder how deep into the city your guide has taken you. A hasty retreat is swiftly declared.
117876:
The yellow tram lurches into movement, starting its trundling jaunt down the street. Suddenly, a cry rings out: an ornate horse-drawn carriage is hurtling towards the crossing! The look of terror on the coachman’s face makes it clear he has lost control of the horse.
With a shudder, the tram stops not three feet from the carriage, startling the creature to a halt. Terrified, it rears impossibly high, its hooves crashing down inches from the carriage.
There is a strange, garbled cry, and a man’s face appears at the window, livid, and with top hat askew, pleading for help.
117878:
A wisp of a girl, only recently part of the crew, sets her face resolutely and edges forward, whispering words of comfort to the panicked creature. Her hand extends to the horse’s chin, turning its eyes away from the metallic sheen of the tram and towards the soft light of a nearby street. Slowly, the animal stills.
The door to the carriage creaks open and a pale man steps uncertainly out. He straightens, and looks at the gathered sailors hazily before paying a low bow, sweeping the dusty street with his top hat.
‘My name is Vasco Oliveira, and in the name of King Joao of Olispo, whom it is my privilege to serve, I pray you accept this small token of thanks.’
117879:
A short, thick-eyed man hesitates, then inches forward to calm the horse — albeit to no avail. It tosses and whinnies furiously, battering the street and rails in a series of metallic clangs which only exacerbates its terror.
A sudden fear gleams in its eye — the carriage lurches into a mad gallop, running over your sailor with a sickening crack and streaming off into the night.
Your surgeon's wounds are serious and must be tended to at once. Heavy-hearted, your crew carry their suffering comrade back to the ship.
117881:
A lanky young topman swiftly reaches into his coat for a carving knife and leaps forward. There's a flash of metal and a snap of leather before the coachman topples back into his seat. The horse whinnies and heads off down the street at a gallop, scaring passersby out of the way. As it rounds the corner, it bowls over a young girl, sending her barrelling into a pile of glaring, dead-eyed, cod, which collapses on her.
However, only then do you remember the stricken cry you heard from inside the carriage.
117883:
A woman with medical knowledge rushes to the girl and kneels by her side.
Pulling her deftly out of the pile of odorous fish, she quickly realizes the girl’s right arm is broken, along with possibly two of her ribs.
She commands some strips of wood and cloth be brought to her, and binds the girl's arm and chest as tightly as possible. It will do until the girl is seen to by more experienced hands.
As the girl's mother steps in to help her daughter up, she insists upon rewarding your crew for their selflessness.
117884:
Emboldened, a sailor leaps off the tram and rushes to help the girl up.. Pain flashes across her face, but your man finds no trace of injury.
‘Why the theatrics, darling?’ he chuckles.
Infuriated, the girl’s mother steps in, shoving the sailor aside.
‘Are you mad, woman?’ he exclaims angrily,
grabbing the girl's arm, intent on proving her health, but a mountain of man steps out from the gathering crowd and deftly locks him in a tight hold.
'Time you left Olispo, senhor...'
His elaborate moustache quivers with repressed anger as he releases his victim and sees you threateningly off into the night.
117886:
One of your crew rushes to the door, swinging it open to reveal a tall man in a ruffled frock coat and top hat. He is unhurt and courteously refuses the outstretched hand to step out of the carriage, taking a deep, steadying breath to gather his composure.
‘A fine show of valour, if perhaps somewhat foolhardy; events might have unfurled very differently. Nevertheless, you succeeded, and for this,’ he doffs his hat to the assembled sailors, bowing low, ‘I, Vasco Oliveira, am much obliged to you.’
117887: Surely you don’t mean Oliveira, the ambassador to King João?
117888: Oliveira? Are you perhaps Vicente Silva’s cousin?
117889: Sure not the Oliveira whose paintings are of notoriously exquisite detail?
117890:
‘The very same, and much honoured to be known by your company! It seems not so long ago I journeyed with some of your countrymen. Pray, do not be startled: it is a small feat indeed for a diplomat such as myself to recognise your accent. I recall your countrymen as amiable fellows, and though we had our differences, we parted in good fellowship.'
He walks to the back of the carriage and opens the trunk.
'Please, accept this small trinket for the sake of better days and friendships not forgotten.’
117891:
A barely hidden scowl flashes across his face.
‘Vicente is my cousin, yes, although why anyone would want to be acquainted with that imbecil is beyond me.' He gives you a cursory glance. I thank you for your efforts, but perhaps it is better that we do not associate any further — clearly you know my cousin too much already.'
With the curtest of bows, he turns away and makes for the fallen girl nearby.
Faces flushed with being publicly dismissed, your crew swiftly head back to the harbour, cursing the fickleness of technology and gentility alike.
117892:
He draws himself up haughtily, his pride evidently pricked.
‘I believe you must be confusing me with the Marques de Oliveira, Adao. A tolerable mistake, had he not been dead twenty years. If you will excuse me, I have matters of a very much living nature to attend to.'
He turns to the coachman, barking a few commands before stepping back into the coach. Already the tale of the foreigners who couldn't tell the living from the dead is spreading like wildfire in not-so-discreet mutterings. This is not what the captain had in mind when he bid you make the Empire proud.
117894:
Time has flown unheeded, and already the hour grows late. The tide waits for no man — nor, for that matter, do the ships’ officers. Your crew drain their last drinks then make their way slowly back to the harbour and the relative comfort of their berths.

When dawn breaks upon the sleeping city, the ship is already picking up speed, its sails taught with the promise of new journeys.
117896:
José casts a disappointed glance upon your crew.
‘I had hoped that seamen would be more adventurous. You would insult us by refusing bread and wine offered in the spirit of friendship? Or are you simply too close-minded?’ He scoffs. ‘You can find your own way out, I am sure.’
Before any of your crew can object, he swivels and disappears into the crowd.
Determined not to conclude the evening on so dispiriting an encounter, you head back to the tram and ride it through the city, back to the harbour through the most circuitous route available, enthusiastically remarking upon the wonders of the modern age between every clank and rumble of the car.
117898:
Your attempts at a Campanilese accent draw a few laughs from surrounding passengers, but the man's insistence on making broken conversation soon becomes trying for all.
One of your men mutters something about him minding his own bloody business — 'don't you have some goats to adopt?'
The native's face flares with fury, rounding on the sulking sailor and answering in your own tongue. 'I tried, but your Queen already has Sir Archibald.'
There is a stunned silence in the tramcar while your crew reel with shock and disgust, before a thick-set young lass leans in and knees him heavily in the midriff, sending him tumbling into a crowd of his outraged countrymen.
117900:
A roar of approval rises from your men as the man sinks to the floor, crimson-faced and groaning. Several burly moustachioed passengers leap into the fray, belts wrapped around their fists, only to be tripped and set upon viciously by sailors eager to vent weeks' worth of restlessness. A whistle sounds through the haze of torn upholstery - the local constabulary!
Your crew promptly jump down from the tram, with a flurry of jabs for good measure, and disperse into the surrounding streets.
117901:
A tram hardly makes for a convenient battle ground. Fists fly into errant faces, drawing bystanders into the brawl and ruining the plush new upholstery. When the coachman finally pulls abruptly on the brakes, sending everyone to the floor, the tramcar more closely resembles a dog-fighting pit than a coach.
Your crew scarper, dispersing through the streets with the shrill whistles of the constabulary hot on their tails. Some are dragged off for a night of holding, and the prospect of public disgrace in the morning.
117902: This is a fight we cannot hope to win
117903:
A wise person chooses their fights carefully — and a sailor, expected to report to duty on the morrow, wounded or not, doubly so.
Your crew hastily disembark from the tramcar, stumbling onto the street, and march back to their fallen comrade, ignoring the jeers and heckling of passengers roused by their aggressor’s anger.
The walk back to the ship seems interminable, and though all agree to turn in for an early night, the gloom of the abandoned festivities hangs heavy in your crew’s heart until the late hours of the night.
117905:
The Empire, eh? It is fortunate you have come on this day, for we are not by nature a forgiving people, and there is much history between us — most of it written in blood. But let us speak no more of this: tonight, we feast and revel; tonight we look to the future! See how swiftly the world changes — why, not a decade ago who would have imagined a tram here? Aye, in years past we drew blood, but tonight we draw wine, and drink to hope, and progress! What say you, por Deus?'
His hearty enthusiasm appears genuine, but you cannot help but wonder how deeply these past grievances are truly buried.
117906: ‘Let the strife of our parents die with them, then. To your good health!'
117907:
A beaming smile lights up his face.
‘Otimo! To a better world, and the bittersweet promise of peace. Let not our forebears cast long shadows over us — to peace!’
He seems to come upon a sudden idea. ‘My name is Alexio, and you must dine with me tonight! We have prepared food aplenty — the finest fare and freshest fish in the entire city, upon my word! Surely you will join us? Such a feast is best shared, and you would be most welcome! It is not every day our city gets its first tram!’
117909:
Alexio takes your eager crew through the streets of Olispo, skilfully weaving in and out of bustling crowds. Torches dance on the azulejos, a strange hypnotic flickering that makes the houses and high walls seem alive with warm, gay colours.
Everywhere, the sounds of chattering laughter, glasses clinking and food being shared fills the air.
A low-hanging door opens onto a bustling taberna — ‘Alexio, at last! We feared the port would run out before you arrived!’
Good cheer lasts well into the night, and dawn finds your crew rich with bonds newly tempered by joyous drinking, and the promise of a brighter future.
117910: Not tonight, friend. The first mate's particular about early rising'
117911:
Obviously crestfallen, but determined to be amicable, Alexio helps the crew navigate a path through the crowds back to the harbour before taking his leave with a wave of his hand. He soon melts back into the throng.
As the last of the crew fall asleep in their berths, they can still hear the din of celebration in the distance, extending well into the small hours of the night.
117912: War is the province of kings, and we will not be pawns in their games'
117913:
He scowls, angrily. ‘What do you know of war, of sacrifice and duty? Many of my kin perished in what you call a game, for what they believed was right.’ His raised voice draws the attention of other patrons, their faces souring as they understand the tenor of the argument. ‘A man's land is his blood, the word of his king his command. I pity you that you cannot understand that.'
He spits contemptuously at your feet, then vanishes into the throng before any retribution can be exacted.
The silence left in his wake is ominous with untold resentment. You try to order a round of port, but the inkeep stares you out of the door.
117914: Only when Olispo has answered for its crimes will we have peace.'
117915:
He bows his head grimly. ‘Foul are the tides of war, and gore-hungry its hounds — none who spill blood can lay claim to righteousness. There are horrors in the past of both our nations. Yet is it not for we who follow to strive to be better? If we can, you and I, have a civil conversation, then perhaps there is still hope for friendship in our nations?
Vamos, let us extend Olispo's hospitality to you, and meet today as brothers rather than foes. To modernity, and peace!’
117916: A noble offer, and one we are glad to accept!
117917:
Alexio takes your eager crew through the streets of Olispo, skilfully weaving in and out of the bustling crowds. Torches and gaslights dance on the azulejos, a strange hypnotic flickering that makes the houses and high walls seem alive with warm, gay colours.
Everywhere, the sound of chattering laughter, glasses clinking against each other and food being shared fills the air.
A low-hanging door opens onto a bustling taberna – ‘Alexio, at last! We feared the port would run out before you arrived!’
Good cheer lasts well into the night, and dawn finds your crew rich with bonds newly tempered by joyous drinking and the promise of a brighter future.
117919: Not tonight, friend; duty calls, and rest
117920:
Obviously crestfallen, but determined to be amicable, Alexio helps the crew navigate a path through the crowds back to the harbour before taking his leave with a wave of his hand. He soon melts back into the throng.
As the last of the crew fall asleep in their berths, they can still hear the din of celebration in the distance, extending well into the small hours of the night.
117922: Any friend of José's is a friend of mine!
117969: The explosion scattered debris across the canal. As your helmsman carefully steers into the nascent Culysma Canal, a deafening blast ahead of you sends most of your crew sprawling across the deck. The initial shock overcome, they rush to their stations and pull the ship into a crawl, bringing it to rest mere feet away from the listing, flame-wracked carcass of a ship. Doubtless it will be days before all is cleansed and navigation can resume. One of your sailors furrows their brow. ‘Innit odd that there en’t no-one in the water?’ Odd indeed — in fact, there's no trace at all of the exploded ship’s crew. An irresistible mystery.
117971:
One of your sailors recalls observing the ship while waiting to enter the canal a few hours ago, noting its peculiar propeller.
Your crew sift through the wreckage in search of the apparatus and find it half-torn from the stern. It is hauled aboard where one of your tradesmen examines it.
‘See the blades? Old models, only ever fitted to a handful o’ ships, and only two of’em so big. My guess is they're from the Innocence— ‘xcept I heard the Crown bought her for salvage not six months past.’
His words slowly sink in. Can the Queen have conspired to sabotage the canal? If local authorities hear of this...
117973:
Fortunately, only a few crew members heard the ghastly secret. All of them are immediately pledged to silence, ‘For Queen and country’.
When their duties have been resumed, your captain sends a carefully worded epistle to Sir Archibald Blake, assuring him of the crew’s loyalty and abnegation in removing any evidence — surely the Queen will reward such loyal subjects!
117974: ‘These people have a right to know.’
117975:
It is a difficult decision to make, but your crew decide to share the information with the Culysma authorities, believing no loyalty should take precedence over righting an injustice.
The canal master thanks your captain profusely, commending his honesty and insisting that your crew be rewarded for their integrity. Before taking his leave, your captain extracts a promise from the grateful official, that no mention will be made to anyone as to the source of the information.
117976:
Sifting through the wreckage without endangering your crew proves to be impossible, as any net used to haul fragments up would be lacerated by the abundance of sharp debris.
After an hour of trying to identify floating fragments, your crew has no choice but to dejectedly relent and turn their backs on the sinking vessel, preparing for a long wait while the authorities clear the canal.
117977: Search nearby for the missing crew.
117978:
Making the most of the long wait ahead, a handful of officers head back to the town nestled at the canal’s entrance. As they near a small eatery by the harbour’s edge, a discussion is overheard in your native language,
‘If we're to keelhaul her, why not take the cargo? Good coin to be made there.’
‘Askin' questions will just get you a beggar’s pension, Konrad. ‘sides, fairly sure the cargo were just there so she blew nice and wide.’
The meaning of what you are hearing sinks in. Could the explosion have been wilful sabotage, and by your countrymen at that? The local authorities ought to be notified, of course, but if these men work for the Crown...
117979:
You dispatch a group of sailors back to Culysma proper to investigate, but it proves too ambitious a task with so few leads to follow. They comb the streets, interrogating locals and mariners as inconspicuously as possible, but the wreck’s crew were either never here, or have long since gone.
By the time the expedition returns to the ship, there is little left to do but wait for the salvage team to clear the canal of debris.
117980: Request ship records from the canal authorities.
117981:
It takes some persuasion, but you convince the officials to let you look into the cargo report for the ship. It reads: FS Deux Freres, h. from Aquiana cleared for crossing this day. Upholstery and tools. Ntd. Nothing salient, yet something feels off, and your sailor quickly remembers: FS? Is that not an Imperial prefix?! Then why register the ship as foreign?

Slowly, it dawns upon you: assuming this is no mistake, does it not imply deliberate sabotage by your own countrymen? It may have implications for the Crown if you were to inform the locals...
117982: The officers manning the canal gates are evidently too busy to recall anything unusual. They answer your captain’s questions willingly enough, at first. The relentlessness of your captain’s questioning, however, slowly distempers them, and they politely but firmly insist that he return to his ship and wait for the salvage crew to finish clearing the canal — any investigation, if investigation there need be, will be undertaken by competent and legal parties.
117988:
Wide, sun-touched lands stretch out before you, long pale grass glittering with the night’s rain while a scattering of trees provides occasional shade from the already warm orange sun.
Unseen amongst the dense, matted grass, multitudinous creatures awake to the dawning day, nattering away gaily as the savannah comes to life.
A low dell not a mile away hides a blossoming waterhole, where numerous strange and foreign beasts are gathering before the day’s heat truly begins, nestled in the shadows of a set of monolithic spurs, looming high above the plains — surely with views worthy of a king!
117989: Scale the spurs for a bird’s eye view of the savannah
117990:
The climb is arduous and long, but your topmen trace a forgeable path for the other sailors, using thick ropes and residues of flour hastily brought over from the camp. At last, you reach the topmost spur — a long slab of ochre red stone, worn by countless rainfalls and storms.

Endless wildlands stretch below you, dust-coloured and windswept. In the distance, rainclouds swirl over a patch of darkness, and a deep golden hush falls over the land, broken only by the slow ambling of strange, tall-collared distant animals. A low threatening growl suddenly echoes behind you, and you turn to face lions, territorially baring their fangs at your crew. You have trespassed upon pride land.
117992:
One gunman shoulders his rifle and takes careful aim at a particularly large male, while the rest of your crew strive to stay as motionless as possible.
The shot echoes deafeningly against the surrounding boulders, and sends a threatening ripple over the lands below.
Cowed by the roar of the rifle and the sight of their pridemate slumping lifeless to the ground, the other lions slowly back away before turning tail and disappearing into the rocks overhead.
117993:
Whether owing to precipitousness or shoddy marksmanship, the shot misses the great creature by several feet.
Panicked, the would be hunter fumbles with the rifle’s lock, but an ominous crack signals the weapon’s reluctance to further use.
The lions take a slow step towards your huddled crew, hunger and wrath in their glare.
‘Someone hold them back!’ cries a sailor, before inching towards the first stone in the long series to climb back to the plains.
117994: Order your two strongest to intimidate the beasts
117995:
Two colossi, nicknamed Ajax and Hercules by your ship’s erudite skipper, step forward.
One of them roars a challenge to the assembled felines, startling them a few steps back into the shadow of the overhanging spur, while the rest of you swiftly start the descent.
As the last of your men slip over the ledge, a low, feral snarl is heard some way overhead. A host of lions have emerged from various crevices and alcoves around Ajax and Hercules — a pride of such size that there is nothing even a hundred men might do to fend them off.
A burst of raucous song comes over the ledge in Ajax’s baritone, and the very next second you see Hercules jump to meet you.'Run!' he says.
117996:
Two burly southerners, thick-necked and ruddy, step forward hesitantly while the rest of your crew slip as discreetly as possible over the ledge and onto the path back to the savannah.
There is a long-minute’s hushed, precipitous silence, before you hear whispers of quiet, nervous conversation up above, followed by an ear-shattering shriek.
One of the men topples over the ledge, plummeting to the distant grassland, as the other becomes the first of many harried by cruel claws and sharp fangs in a fraught and fearful descent.
117998:
Years of experience are easily forgotten in the face of mortal peril. Your sailors push and pull at each other to be first to descend onto the lower ledges, and away from the rampant cats.
One man stumbles and falls with a sickening crack onto the stone, blood soon clotting his hair and pooling on the dark red rock.
The smell of blood inflames the lions, and what reservations they had are forgotten, pouncing upon the stragglers, rending them to pieces. Pride's rock is a name whose irony will not be lost on your expedition.
117999: Throw the cabin boy to the lions
118008: Bos taurus. Ten thousand years our allies.
118012: Tranquil giants with an eternal memory of their home.
118014: Worth the five men it took to catch.
118015: Speak softly and carry a big stick.
118016: The movement entrusts you part of their territory.
118017: One sheep, two sheep, three sheep ...
118025: The finest selection of animals will make your city far more attractive.
118026: This enclosure can house any animal.
118030: Grows sugar cane in farm fields.
118031: Only useful if equipped with items. Attach items here to provide bonuses to production.
118032: Responds to fires within range. Can mobilise additional units.
118033:
The captain knows he must do what is right. Do the lives of the many not outweigh the lives of the few — and are sturdy, aged hands not valued more in a storm than those of a youngling?
Yet the cabin boy’s wan, stricken face haunts him long after the garbled, bloodied crying — horrifyingly close, despite the distance — falls silent, at the claws of a merciful beast. None of your crew know untroubled sleep for many a week.
118034: Intimidate the beasts with loud noises and gestures
118035:
Acting as one, your crew start stamping the ground rhythmically, battering the stone with such force that it trembles while fiercely waving their arms in large circles, concealing their terror as best they can.
Startled, the lions slowly edge backwards, their low growls no longer threatening but worried, and promptly disband, gracefully bounding up among the stunted prickly bushes where their den must be hidden.
118036: Corner the den and smoke the beasts in
118037:
Dry wood and kindle abound despite recent rainfalls, and a series of short pyres are built around the lair’s entrance. Soon, bright flames cast deep shadows far back into the cave.
Rain-soaked grass and leaves are thrown onto the fires, spurting voluminous columns of creamy grey smoke.
There is a moment’s silence as the fumes invade the lair, before a powerful shape leaps through the haze — only to be caught by those lying in wait.
The lion roars its fury and anguish, to no avail, and your crew quickly return to camp, triumphantly bragging about their prize.
118038:
Finding kindle dry enough to start a fire proves difficult atop pride’s rock, especially with recent rains. You struggle to light small piles of damp grass and twigs, but your efforts only attract the lions’ attention. A female leaps toward a man struggling with a tinder box.
He ducks backward, narrowly avoiding a killing blow, only for blood to spurt to the ground as a ghastly tear appears in his jaw, his teeth visible through the wound. Your crew take cover behind what small, flickering torches they've managed to light, and start the achingly slow descent back to the plains, with their gored companion in tow.
118040:
Preferring to err on the side of safety, your captain orders a swift retreat down the spur, while the pride is cowed and cautious.
Evening finds you all huddled around the campfire, exaggeratedly recounting the encounter with the pride to those sailors who had stayed behind.
A sudden cry of wild dogs is heard distantly in the night, and you wonder at the beauty and majesty of this foreign land, strangely satisfied with the bloodlessness of your expedition.
118041: The pride is undeterred by your efforts to shout and stomp them away. Ignoring the increasingly high-pitched cries sallying from your crew, they prowl up to the edge of the overhanging slab, preparing to pounce. You look around at your crew, but the expedition up the spur seemed so harmless that none of them brought a rifle— save one lean and dark-faced young woman, who carries a narrow-barreled pistol model from overseas at her side. You feel entirely comfortable resting your odds of survival upon that. Cornering the lions when they land to subdue them might be easier, or repelling them with a hail of rocks?
118042: Prepare to corner them when they land
118043:
You order a loosening of the ranks — if the beasts pounce, they should immediately be surrounded —and not a moment too soon, as one particularly impressive male leaps into the fray. You prepare to corner it when a powerful fist crashes into the side of the beast’s head mid-leap, sending it sprawling, dazed, several feet away.
Surprised at the strength of Ajax, a surly but powerfully muscular gunman, your crew hastily retreat off the spur while the lion is stunned, and its companions cowed.
Tales abound around the campfire that night of the mighty feat of Ajax, without entirely making up for the crew’s sensation that they only narrowly escaped with their lives.
118044: One of the lions pounces upon a young man in the front ranks. He ducks, hoping to avoid the beast, but sharp claws rake into his shoulder, blood spurting violently as the lad crashes down under the creature’s weight. His companions pummel the lion with their fists, but it barely seems to acknowledge the blows, and busies itself with goring the unfortunate lad. All pretence of resistance finally abandons your crew; broken, the sailors disband and flee back to the savannah, routed and haunted by the dreadful fate of their young comrade.
118045: Order the woman to shoot, and hope that the gun works
118046:
Her face breaks into a dark grin as she draws the pistol to her hip with lightning speed. Sunlight glares off the silvery metal as rapid-fire shots flare from the muzzle with deadly precision and speed.
There is a moment's unbelieving, bated silence as four lions crumble to the dust, blood oozing from the small round wounds in their foreheads.
The woman smiles, satisfied, before returning her pistol to its holster with a flourish. A roar of whoops and cheers rises from your crew, and as they wend their way down from the spur, they crowd the sharpshooter to hear of her pistol — the last of the bolt six-shooters — and already, the legend of the woman who drew faster than her own shadow spreads like wildfire.
118047:
She draws the weapon with great haste, however, only one of the six rapid-fire shots hits its target. The lion roars, its mane matted by fast-flowing blood, while its companions furiously pounce on the young woman. Powerful jaws close with a sickening crack on her skull, bursting it open in a splatter of gore which sends surrounding sailors reeling and vomiting.
A famished growl is heard from above, before a newly woken group of slavering beasts jumps into the fray, rending with teeth and claw as your crew run for their lives.
118048: Throw a volley of stones at them
118049: You stoop hurriedly to grab a series of sharp rocks, pelting them towards the approaching creatures. They back away without breaking eye contact, clearly weathering the storm until there comes a chance to resume their hunt. Some issue low growls as the rocks hit their flanks, but most seem unworried.
118051:
Some of your crew weep to see vital supplies tossed to the beasts, but all agree that they would rather lose food than become food.
The offering pacifies the pride long enough for your sailors to head quickly back down the spur — a terrifying encounter, certainly, but one that is sure to reward them with many an admiring drink in the pub back home.
118052: You had expected to be back at camp by noon, and consequently brought very little food along — hardly enough to placate the hungering lions. Perhaps it is merely your imagination, but you think you hear a low rumbling run through the dark rock, as beasts from all corners draw threateningly closer.
118054:
Your party edges stealthily through the high grass towards the hidden waterhole. As they reach a ledge where soft soil has fallen into the muddy water below, they gasp in wonder at the teeming life gathered here. Scores of creatures huddle by the water — tall-necked giraffes spread their legs awkwardly to lean down and lap the surface, while nervous meerkats and contemptuous gnus eye the waters warily — and with the suspicious profile of those drifting logs, it's not without reason.
Suddenly, the ground shakes. You wheel about to see a manifestly infuriated rhinoceros charging at your company!
118056:
Your crew scatter as one tall woman, made lean by years of working in the rigging, steps up out of the grass to face the charging beast. She straightens proudly, defiance flashing in her eyes, and waits for the inevitable blow.
At the last instant, she steps gracefully aside, sending the beast hurtling into the thick tree behind her. Stunned by the impact, the rhinoceros staggers slightly, shaking its head to extricate its horn from the torn flesh of the tree.
118058:
Several sailors nimbly tie the creature’s legs together, carefully avoiding its thrashing head. The rhinoceros struggles against the binding, kicking out violently, but your men tug on the ropes and the beast comes crashing down on its side, motionless but fuming.
It takes considerable effort to drag it back to camp, but the dumbfounded look on the rest of the crew’s face is worth every bead of sweat.
118059: By the time ropes are brought out to secure it, the rhinoceros has already struggled free of the tree and rounds furiously at the oncoming sailors. They attempt as best they can to bind its legs, dancing dangerously in and out of a flurry of rearing and kicking, but the massive creature proves impossible to subdue, and it's not long before it surges out of the encirclement, thundering off into the savannah, much to your crew’s disappointment.
118061:
A horde of gnus stampede past your crew, evidently alarmed by the thunderous attack of the rhinoceros, separating you from the beast.
Leaping upon the opportunity to escape the maddened creature and its threatening bulk, you promptly retreat back to camp, thrilled by your escape — and the impressively dramatic skills of the woman who deceived the rhinoceros.
118062:
Your captain singles out a sailor renowned for manoeuvring rigging in heavy storms, and orders him to lure the beast into a nearby tree.
The man stands nervously, his terror evident as the rhinoceros bowls right into his path. He tries to lurch aside at the last minute, only to be skewered by the beast’s impressive nasal horn.
A terrified roar rises from the nearby waterhole as the gathered animals sense the gore and panic, their anxiety soon turning into a stampede! The few crew members that do escape the terror-stricken beasts will be forever traumatised.
118065:
Years of seamanship, climbing the rigging of a moving, storm-tossed ship, makes scaling low, twisted trees only a minor challenge.
The rhinoceros tromps to a halt when it realises its quarry has vanished, looking around with dull, rage-shot eyes before retreating into the sun-worn high grass.
As the sailors ease down from their hiding places, they dejectedly realise that the creature’s tonitruous charge has chased all the animals from the waterhole, and there is naught left to do but retreat back to camp.
118066:
The crew scramble for low branches and scalable knots in the thick, tortuous trunks of the surrounding trees. Most find easy purchase and disappear into the dense foliage, but a few are left attempting to scale a young silver-barked tree; supple and tall, but clearly unable to bear all their weight. They tussle for a foothold as the rumble of the rhinoceros’s charge grows nearer.
A third man attempts to hoist himself up, but his companions push him roughly, only to see the chap tumble into the beast's charge.
Satisfied that it has repelled its attackers, the animal leaves, but only after consciously trampling the body in full sight of every crew member, a scene that will haunt them until their dying days.
118068:
It is well known among naturalists that rhinoceroses have limited vision, and the information is quickly doled out to your crew in whispers. Taking great care to avoid sudden movements, all move out of the creature’s immediate path and adopt resolute stillness.
The beast grinds to a halt when it realises its foes have vanished. It tosses and turns its voluminous head, eyeing the high undergrowth for any sign of life.
After a long, breathy moment of indecision, it finally turns away and tromps down to the waterhole, to take in long, slow draughts of water.
118069:
Your attempts to convince the sailors to stay motionless would have been more efficient had four thousand pounds of armoured, horn-touting, furious beast not been hurtling towards them. One lad, seeing the beast drawing ever nearer, gives in to fear and breaks into a mad escape.
The rhinoceros immediately turns towards him, and your crew seize the opportunity to retreat, desperately trying to ignore the fact that in order to escape, the young man's life will be forfeit.
118072: Flee as far as you can
118073:
Attempts to outrun the rhinoceros are futile. Turning to the stragglers, it singles out a limping fellow and bellows, before charging and skewering him with its horn.
As the body of their crewmate is tossed and broken underfoot, your sailors flee back to camp, haunted by visions of a dark, bloodied horn piercing through the man’s abdomen in a spurt of gore.
118074: Encircle the beast to confuse it
118075: Rhinoceroses are swift, but their bulk lends them poor mobility. Your crew dance in and out of the beast’s vision, leaving it dizzily turning from one evanescent figure to the next. As soon as it is sufficiently dazed, your men dart behind the creature’s colossal backside and run hurriedly back to camp, hidden by tall grass, fearing at every instant they might hear a furious bellow, catch a glimpse of grey armour, or feel the sharp end of that osseous horn.
118076: Much rather their stomachs be filled with this food than with you
118081:
You order a loosening of the ranks — if the beasts pounce, they should immediately be surrounded —and not a moment too soon, as one particularly impressive male leaps into the fray. You prepare to corner it when a powerful fist crashes into the side of the beast’s head mid-leap, sending it sprawling, dazed, several feet away.
Surprised at the strength of Ajax, a surly but powerfully muscular gunman, your crew hastily retreat off the spur while the lion is stunned, and its companions cowed.
Tales abound around the campfire that night of the mighty feat of Ajax, without entirely making up for the crew’s sensation that they only narrowly escaped with their lives.
118082: One of the lions pounces upon a young man in the front ranks. He ducks, hoping to avoid the beast, but sharp claws rake into his shoulder, blood spurting violently as the lad crashes down under the creature’s weight. His companions pummel the lion with their fists, but it barely seems to acknowledge the blows, and busies itself with goring the unfortunate lad. All pretence of resistance finally abandons your crew; broken, the sailors disband and flee back to the savannah, routed and haunted by the dreadful fate of their young comrade.
118084:
Guns are nervously loaded and trained on the creatures, when a sudden burst of rapid-fire shots sallies from the rear ranks of your crew. Three of the lions stumble before falling at your feet, heads bloodied by uncannily precise sharpshooting.
The remaining lions back away in terror as your crew wisely head back down the spur, gushing proudly about the young shooter’s skills, yet unpleasantly aware of how narrowly they just avoided death.
118085:
Your crew fumble to load their weapons, and a volley of haphazard shots crackles through the warm air. Without the proper time to aim, the marksmen miss the beasts by several feet.
Enraged, the lions pounce, ripping and goring those nearby with powerful maws, spattering blood through the air and onto the rest of your horrified party. Abandoning all pretence of bravery, they flee the towering rocks, followed by the dying cries of their comrades.
118086: The Last Tale of Ta Netjer
118087:
One of the lower halyards suddenly snaps, lashing through the air with serpentine speed as the sail it was shackling swells with the seasonal winds. The ship lurches hard to port, cutting through strange mists until, with a resounding squeal, the keel grinds to a halt on pebble-scattered shores.
Scores of minute piles of pale sand are scattered across the beach — thousands upon thousands of wispy pyramidia, stretching up to the woodlands beyond.
Dark shapes jut out of the sand irregularly; fragments of ancient derelict and long-forgotten vessels, carefully preserved in brine and surf. Perhaps something of their tale may yet be found on this strangest of islands?
118090:
Your captain kneels to brush one of the ankle-high piles, and is surprised to find his touch met by the resistance of water-logged sand.
The pyramidion suddenly collapses inward, and a great crab sallies forth from the rubble, golden-caparisoned and fierce, its white claw as broad as a man’s palm.
Ignoring your captain completely, the creature scuttles into the water and disappears among the surf. Once their wits have returned, your crew realise each pile must host a similar critter, and collect as many as possible to cook over a fire.
As they relish the flavoursome sweet flesh, one of them sights a collection of splendidly silhouetted houses, high on a jutting spur, with sunlight catching their tile roofs.
118091:
The trees here stretch into tortuous shapes,clad in alien-hued pale greens and cream barks. Thick bushes grow errantly across the dust-swathed stone plain, while short funnel-barrelled trees loom over them. One genus particularly strikes your fancy: its dense branches stretch up like arms toward the sky, cupping the close foliage into dark green umbrellas, its bark torn and oozing a dark, blood-like resin.

A smile of relish spreads on one crewman's face as he discovers its plump fruit to be ripe. All gather around, gorging upon the fallen fruit, when a woman points out the silhouette of distant houses on a mountainous plateau.
118092: Send a team to scale the mountains
118094:
The sharp biting rock makes for an arduous climb over these often sheer bluffs. Fragile limestone ledges, weakened by many centuries of briny winds, crumble underfoot despite your crew’s experience. As you round one particularly ominous spur of the cliff, a cry rings out: unstable rocks have given way, swiftly tumbling into a landslide which sweeps away one sailor after another.

When at last the dust settles, you find the landslide has brought you to a dark chamber. Soft waters gently lap against unwary boots, and the dark sheen of a brackish subterranean lake gleams through a forest of stalagmited passages, weaving an eerie maze into the gloom.
118095:
Small, gold-winged finches roost lazily among the thick-woven branches of strange stout trees, while lizards, large enough to fill a bucket, unblinkingly follow your crew’s progress through the brush.

Once upon a time, a long, long, time ago, a king had only one son, renowned for being kind and compassionate to all.

The lion's jaw fell open in surprise! "I've never met a human who isn't scared of me. Much less a human willing to share their meal with me!"
The prince responded, "We should always show a kind heart. Everyone deserves compassion, whether they be sheep, human or lion."
Impressed by these wise words, the lion decided to accompany the prince to his kingdom. The prince became a beloved king, and the lion remained his great friend for the rest of their lives - and that is why the lion is the symbol of our nation.
119377:
"Eat me now, and the honey will stick your jaw shut!" exclaimed the prince. The lion sighed, annoyed "I'll just wait for the honey to dry, then I'll eat you."
"A fair point...", conceded the prince, "In the meantime, tell me: what's it like being a lion?"
Intrigued by the question, the lion and the prince talked for so long that by the time the honey dried, the lion didn't want to eat the prince any more. The conflict resolved, the prince offered the lion a place by his side, and thus it became the symbol of our nation.
119378:
In a matter of minutes, the prince had extracted enough water for the shepherdess's whole family. He helped her carry it to her house where he met with her father, a poor, old man who had little to offer by way of thanks, but insisted that the prince stay the night. Exhausted by the ordeal, the prince gladly accepted.
In the middle of the night, however, the prince was awakened by some low, hissing sounds. Still quite tired, he sat up to ask for some peace, but froze when he saw two enormous pale snakes by his bed.
Despite the danger, however, the prince kept his composure and... hum...

119381:
Reaching for the sword by his pillow, the prince struck out and beheaded both snakes with one blow! But as they dropped to the floor, their bodies shifted, revealing two very young, and now very dead men. Alerted by the noise, the old man hobbled into the room and started weeping at the sight. "My boys! What have you done! You seemed so kind-hearted, I thought you would help them! But now... how could you!"
Red-faced with shame and remorse, the prince fled the hovel at once and went back to his father's palace, swearing to the Heavens that he would never again judge by appearance, and would remain a friend to all, human or otherwise.
119382:
"You... you do not fear us?" the surprised snakes asked.
"Why should I?" answered the prince. "We are all the Lord's creatures, and you deserve as much respect as any other."
Upon hearing these words, the snakes' skin blurred and hazed, and soon two young boys stood in their stead. "Father, father!" one of them cried in glee. The old man rushed out of the house and wept to see his sons. "I knew it! Only one as wise as you could treat them with humanity and break the curse! A thousand blessings to a prince with such kindness in his heart!"
Soon, news of the prince's wisdom had spread throughout the land, and all praised him, striving to follow his example, and not judge anyone so readily.

TRANSLATED FROM THE ENBESAN

Biniam my love,

Mother hasn't heard from you in a while, and is heart-sick with worry, so do please write. I am sure you've not forgotten me here by the wasi, as you have always been such an attentive boy — always helping mother cook and clean the livelong years. I am sure you must simply be so time-busy with Janihoy Ketema's plans for Taborime, and this important visitor from afar.

Perhaps your plan for the Research Institute has met with approval! Oh yes indeed — I cling to the thought that such things keep you from me, and that no misfortune is the cause of this sudden silence between us. My affection-wishes as always.

Your mother, Kyria.

120549:
You dock at a small, lively port on the northern coast. While most of your crew replenish supplies and repair the damage suffered in a recent storm, some decide to head off to explore the local souq.

Streets fold and unfold into each other, bedecked in a wild array of colours and dizzyingly heady unknown scents, which so confuse your sailors that they become lost in the weave of passages. Seeing their distress, several young men in beggarly clothes offer to guide them through the maze.
120550: Shoo them off and trust your crew’s instincts.
120551:
It takes some observation, but your sailors soon understand that the mosaic of low-hanging cloths are arranged in specific patterns. A sharp right after a spice dealer’s enthusiastic attempt to sell your crew a few years’ worth of ochre and red powders leads them to a small, shadowed plaza, where two musicians are strumming many-stringed zithers of rich-honeyed wood.
There is a peacefulness to this place that soothes your crew, and they try to engage the musicians in conversation to learn more about their culture.
120552: Attempt to hail them in their native tongue.
120553:
Your crew’s linguistic efforts attract much appreciative surprise, and a lively conversation soon sparks up, supplemented by voluminous approximative sign language and much laughter.
Before your sailors can object, an intricate tea set is brought out, and the small pewter cups are soon brimming with steaming, crisp-scented mint tea, supplemented by flavoursome pastries. Many tales are traded, and nightfall has long since passed when your crew return to the ship, arms laden with simple but intricate tokens of friendship.
120554: Your crew barely knows enough of the language to greet the locals, let alone carry their questions. After a few long minutes of polite puzzlement, they courteously but pointedly turn away. Frustrated, your crew retreat to the ship, hoping the next port encountered will be slightly more cosmopolitan.
120555: Gesticulate to try and convey your meaning.
120556: Not wishing to interrupt the music, one sailor walks up to a man about to enter a nearby house and taps his shoulder to attract his attention. The man turns a curious face to this unexpected intervention.
120557: Gesture between your mouth and the man, indicating you wish to speak to him.
120558: The man’s face darkens with anger. He barks a few clearly offensive words and strides across the threshold, slamming the door in your crew’s baffled faces. Judging by the condemning stares they now attract, your sailors understand the gesture they made is considered a great insult, and wisely decide to retreat to the ship before committing another faux pas.
120559: Point out the surroundings and give a thumbs up, indicating you find his home beautiful.
120560: The man starts unpleasantly, visibly insulted, before casting a witheringly contemptuous glare at your expectant crew. Judging by the condemning stares they are suddenly attracting, your sailors understand the gesture must have some unknown, possibly derogatory meaning here, and wisely decide to retreat to the ship before committing another faux pas.

120562:
The man smiles, and a conversation slowly begins, accompanied by a smattering of local idioms and considerable use of sign language. Understanding your crew to be foreign, he promptly invites them in and welcomes them with generous helpings of piping mint tea and soft, honeyed pastries.
When your crew part ways with him, they cannot help but feel comfort in the knowledge such friendships, beyond words and shared history, may still be found.
120563:
It is not long before your crew are hopelessly lost in the tangle of crowded streets. From all parts, merchants assail them with hopeful voices, flaunting the quality of their wares and the attractiveness of their prices in such a way that the sailors soon feel like a sloop buffeted by harsh winds.
One particularly bold and smiling merchant walks up to the lead sailor.
‘I have just the thing for you — rare items, impossible to find elsewhere!’
His wares seem common enough, but perhaps he can give you directions?
120564: Try to secure his help by purchasing something.
120565: Tahanina! You have an eye for fine items!
120568:
The tradeoff hardly seems fair, but your sailors are eager to find a way out of the souq. Once the deal is concluded, the grinning merchant points them to a low set of arched doors nearby that will lead them back to the safety of the harbour.
Your crew try to convince themselves, loudly and unconvincingly, that the bauble will at least make for a decent souvenir, despite its hefty cost.
120569:
You try to haggle the prices down to something reasonable, but it becomes increasingly clear that the merchant has little intention of making an honest deal. This suspicion is confirmed when, after a particularly vehement refusal to pay a fortune for what looks like common kitchenware, he barks a few short words.
Immediately, several burly individuals appear through the draperies at the back of the shop. With a chill, you realise the price to pay has just increased steeply!
120571: How pleasant to deal with reasonable people!
120574:
The merchant can barely hide his glee as you hand over the outrageous fee he has just extorted from you. He waves a sardonic goodbye, as his acolytes lead your crew back through the crowded souq to the docks.
Once back aboard the ship, it becomes very tempting to throw the thing overboard, but the officers insist it be kept, tacking a note to it reading ‘Now you know why shore leave is restricted.’

120577:
Outnumbered though they may be, your sailors settle in for a fight, some of them drawing ribbing knives and various crude but wickedly-edged items from the pockets of their breeches. The thugs' faces fall, discountenanced by these weapons — evidently, they were not prepared for so hostile a reaction, and so safely back a few paces away, behind the dais.
Furious at his men’s cowardice, the merchant has no choice but to mumble directions to the harbour, leaving your crew to operate a swift retreat.

The ship’s boy rounds on him angrily.
‘Stop bein’ a bloody pain and scram!’
The man’s expression sours, and he steps forward and grabs the lad by the collar. Before anyone can react, your crew realize the altercation has attracted a crowd of hostile locals, some of them reaching for long knives.

Cowed and bruised, the thugs slink back to side streets, as your crew operate a hasty retreat to the safety of the ship.

Unwilling to tarry any longer, your crew turn heels and flee the scene, cheeks burning with the trailing sound of scornful hilarity.

Ignoring the outstretched wares, one of your sailors uses what little she knows of the local language to ask the man for the quickest path to the harbour.
He flounders, evidently conflicted, before mumbling a series of nigh-incomprehensible directions.
Your crew follow them as best they can, but whether due to their cryptic nature, or to your sailors’ general ineptitude in terms of orientation, it takes them the better part of the afternoon to find a way out of the souq and back onto the ship.

120593:
One of your crew members singles out a promising intellectual, with sleeves intricately patterned with dark arabesque lines. It is only when he eagerly draws nearer that you realise the lines are actually inked directly upon his skin — the verses of holy texts in his native script.

It is evident that he is well-learned despite his lowly means, and so helpful is he in describing the lore and history of the city that your diplomat cannot help but be impressed by his earnestness. When the time comes to pay him, your sailor instead offers him an apprenticeship, with your captain’s approval.The young man, however, is reticent, and claims his elderly family could not provide for itself without him.
120594: Insist upon meeting his family in the hope of convincing them
120595:
The man’s home is barely more than a hovel, tucked away in an alcove on one of the narrower kuchehs threading the souq. His parents greet you worried, offering bland tea with oft-infused leaves, and it pains you to think it is probably the best they have to offer.
The debate is long and heated, with much arguing back and forth: the elderly couple are evidently worried as to their fate when they can no longer provide for themselves. However it is with a heavy heart that they ultimately relent and give him their blessing, imploring you to care for him as one of your own.
120596:
You follow the young man to a small, crowded room in one of the riads overlooking the market, where an aged couple greet you tersely. Their mood darkens as soon as they understand that you are asking to take their son away, and they firmly turn down your many arguments and offers.
‘The Book says the young must support the aged in the dusk of their life. Who are you to deny this?’ You think to reply that their son is no spring chicken himself, but
sensing their resolve, you have no choice but to relent and bid him a disappointed farewell.
120597: Insist: such talent should not be wasted.
120598:
Flattered at first, the man soon wearies of your insistence.
‘I have duties here, and a family to care for. Your offer does you credit, but what are promises made by strangers newly met, however honourable, in the eyes of the duty imparted by the Almighty? My place is here.’
His tone as he finishes giving you a tour of the city is cooler, but when you part ways, he smiles, and you reward him generously for his expertise.
120599: Respect his conviction and sense of duty.
120600:
No man should feel compelled to loftier destinies if their duty calls them elsewhere. Your crew compliment him on his sense of loyalty to his kin, and tip him handsomely for his guidance and company.
By way of a parting gift, he traces a few elegant lines on a small piece of paper — an errant verse from a poem he is working on — before disappearing back into the souq.
Roughly translated, the line reads ‘Mine was a life divinely ordained, and thus I knew serenity’, and is signed with the lad’s name, Qaddr Razzaq.

The men throng around you in a clamour of self-professed learnedness and helpfulness. Overwhelmed, you select a young man whose confidence and insistence seem to make him a wise option.
It is soon painfully obvious, however, that he was a poor choice. Though he does take you through the colourful and bustling souq, he has little to say about it, and his pace is brisk.
After an hour of so, you reach a remote and secluded part of the market, only to have him turn to you sombrely, declaring his guided tour complete and demanding an extortionate fee for his services.

120603: Surely you were not expecting my services to be free?
