Reluctantly, you hand over the hefty sum, and he deftly pockets it before disappearing into a nearby alley, leaving your crew to find their own way back to the ship — only now with lighter purses, and much animosity towards the locals.
120607: Visibly upset at being denied his due, the young man starts chattering angrily in his native tongue. Your crew attempt to leave the place and find their own way back to the harbour through the stench of nearby tanneries, but your guide follows your every footstep, insisting upon being paid in increasingly loud and aggressive tones. You attempt to ignore him, but his relentlessness is sorely testing your crew's patience.
120608: Attempt to intimidate and scare him away.
120609:
One of your sailors lashes out angrily at the young man, cuffing him sharply behind the head. ‘Learn your place, boy!’
He staggers slightly, dazed and shocked, terror welling up in his gaze. Before anyone can step in, he ducks behind a great vat of bubbling dyes and flees your sailors’ wrath.
While navigating a path back to the harbour, your crew cannot help but feel guilty at their treatment of the boy — when one is so abjectly destitute, it is little surprise that propriety should bow to need.
120610:
One of your sailors steps threateningly towards the boy, reaching out to grab him by the front of his ragged shirt. The lad, however, darts nimbly out of reach, colliding with another surprised sailor before leaping behind a high stratified stack of drying tea leaves. When your men round it, much to the protest of the labourers tending the stack, the lad has disappeared.
As your crew uncertainly head back to the harbour, the man the boy had run into cries out: his belt pouch is missing, evidently stolen!
120611: The lad clearly needs to be taught the error of his ways.
120612:
‘It is natural that securing your basic needs should take precedence over your absolute moral being. But there are resources in the province of lawfulness that you could abide by...' and so on and so forth.
Your sailor’s benevolent, albeit pompous tones have some tempering effect on the lad, but when the lecture is over, you cannot help but wonder how much of it he understood, yet alone took to heart.
120613:
‘Never is there cause to be immoral, lest the principle of morality be neutered. If society is to be society and justice to be justice, there can be no legitimate unlawfulness, and consequently, you must reflect on your immorality and change your ways.’
The young man’s face darkens with every self-important word, and he swiftly turns heel on your sailor, stranding him mid-speech.
As your crew return to the ship, a series of angry mutterings arise from all parts, and a hail of broken earthenware rains down from high windows.
Your crew suffer numerous cuts and bruises.
120619:
The lights of Olispo glimmer through the spray as your sailors hasten to secure their mooring. Music and merriment spill from the narrow streets, wafting aromas of warm bread and savoury fish fresh from the tide.
With a thrill of pent up anticipation, the sailors stream off the ship and excitedly crowd onto a pristinely new yellow tram, laughing as it rickets off into the warm night, hailed loudly by festive locals.
A flurry of ample sleeves turns to them genially:
'Boa noite, friends! From whence does the tide bring you?'
120621:
‘Maravilhoso! I have kin there — wonderful people, and hardworking to a fault!
Come, we must drink — and I know just the place. Follow me!’
The sailors clamber off the tram gracelessly, unaccustomed to its peculiar rhythm, before following the man through a maze of passages lit by antique oil lamps hanging from balconies. Stopping before a low stone arch, he reaches through the overgrown ivy, pulling open an unseen door.
A flare of chattering and low lights greets you, wafting dark-scented spirits and fresh-roasted food.‘Try the pasteis de nata, our sweet, secret custardy pride! And of course, our famous port!'
120622: Order a generous round of port and custard pies
120623: Any friend of José's is a friend of mine!
120626:
The innkeeper navigates the thronged room expertly, avoiding boisterous patrons to set a large platter onto the table. Your crew swiftly attack the warm pastries, wolfing down the soft custard with aplomb, while Jose introduces a merry waltz of friends, each eager to toast the newcomers to their city.
When the festivities peter out in the late hours of the night, your sailors trickle back the ship, full-bellied, light-headed and free of care.
120627:
The innkeeper scoffs when your crew remark on the price.
‘This is no mere city, amigos. This is Olispo, land of riches and flavour! Surely you do not expect to feast for free!’
There's a minute of long, awkward silence before Jose, obviously crestfallen, clears his throat. Clearly, he had hoped his helpfulness would earn him a night of free food and drink.
With a curt bow and a ‘Boa noite’, he steps out into the night.
Suddenly the crowd seems much less amicable, and you cannot help but wonder how deep into the city your guide has taken you. A hasty retreat is swiftly declared.
120629:
The yellow tram lurches into movement, starting its trundling jaunt down the street. Suddenly, a cry rings out: an ornate horse-drawn carriage is hurtling towards the crossing! The look of terror on the coachman’s face makes it clear he has lost control of the horse.
With a shudder, the tram stops not three feet from the carriage, startling the creature to a halt. Terrified, it rears impossibly high, its hooves crashing down inches from the carriage.
There is a strange, garbled cry, and a man’s face appears at the window, livid, and with top hat askew, pleading for help.
120631:
A wisp of a girl, only recently part of the crew, sets her face resolutely and edges forward, whispering words of comfort to the panicked creature. Her hand extends to the horse’s chin, turning its eyes away from the metallic sheen of the tram and towards the soft light of a nearby street. Slowly, the animal stills.
The door to the carriage creaks open and a pale man steps uncertainly out. He straightens, and looks at the gathered sailors hazily before paying a low bow, sweeping the dusty street with his top hat.
‘My name is Vasco Oliveira, and in the name of King Joao of Olispo, whom it is my privilege to serve, I pray you accept this small token of thanks.’
120632:
A short, thick-eyed man hesitates, then inches forward to calm the horse — albeit to no avail. It tosses and whinnies furiously, battering the street and rails in a series of metallic clangs which only exacerbates its terror.
A sudden fear gleams in its eye — the carriage lurches into a mad gallop, running over your sailor with a sickening crack and streaming off into the night.
Your surgeon's wounds are serious and must be tended to at once. Heavy-hearted, your crew carry their suffering comrade back to the ship.
120634:
A lanky young topman swiftly reaches into his coat for a carving knife and leaps forward. There's a flash of metal and a snap of leather before the coachman topples back into his seat. The horse whinnies and heads off down the street at a gallop, scaring passersby out of the way. As it rounds the corner, it bowls over a young girl, sending her barrelling into a pile of glaring, dead-eyed, cod, which collapses on her.
However, only then do you remember the stricken cry you heard from inside the carriage.
120636:
A woman with medical knowledge rushes to the girl and kneels by her side.
Pulling her deftly out of the pile of odorous fish, she quickly realizes the girl’s right arm is broken, along with possibly two of her ribs.
She commands some strips of wood and cloth be brought to her, and binds the girl's arm and chest as tightly as possible. It will do until the girl is seen to by more experienced hands.
As the girl's mother steps in to help her daughter up, she insists upon rewarding your crew for their selflessness.
120637:
Emboldened, a sailor leaps off the tram and rushes to help the girl up.. Pain flashes across her face, but your man finds no trace of injury.
‘Why the theatrics, darling?’ he chuckles.
Infuriated, the girl’s mother steps in, shoving the sailor aside.
‘Are you mad, woman?’ he exclaims angrily,
grabbing the girl's arm, intent on proving her health, but a mountain of man steps out from the gathering crowd and deftly locks him in a tight hold.
'Time you left Olispo, senhor...'
His elaborate moustache quivers with repressed anger as he releases his victim and sees you threateningly off into the night.
120639:
One of your crew rushes to the door, swinging it open to reveal a tall man in a ruffled frock coat and top hat. He is unhurt and courteously refuses the outstretched hand to step out of the carriage, taking a deep, steadying breath to gather his composure.
‘A fine show of valour, if perhaps somewhat foolhardy; events might have unfurled very differently. Nevertheless, you succeeded, and for this,’ he doffs his hat to the assembled sailors, bowing low, ‘I, Vasco Oliveira, am much obliged to you.’
120640: Surely you don’t mean Oliveira, the ambassador to King João?
120641:
‘The very same, and much honoured to be known by your company! It seems not so long ago I journeyed with some of your countrymen. Pray, do not be startled: it is a small feat indeed for a diplomat such as myself to recognise your accent. I recall your countrymen as amiable fellows, and though we had our differences, we parted in good fellowship.'
He walks to the back of the carriage and opens the trunk.
'Please, accept this small trinket for the sake of better days and friendships not forgotten.’
120642: Oliveira? Are you perhaps Vicente Silva’s cousin?
120643:
A barely hidden scowl flashes across his face.
‘Vicente is my cousin, yes, although why anyone would want to be acquainted with that imbecil is beyond me.' He gives you a cursory glance. I thank you for your efforts, but perhaps it is better that we do not associate any further — clearly you know my cousin too much already.'
With the curtest of bows, he turns away and makes for the fallen girl nearby.
Faces flushed with being publicly dismissed, your crew swiftly head back to the harbour, cursing the fickleness of technology and gentility alike.
120644: Sure not the Oliveira whose paintings are of notoriously exquisite detail?
120645:
He draws himself up haughtily, his pride evidently pricked.
‘I believe you must be confusing me with the Marques de Oliveira, Adao. A tolerable mistake, had he not been dead twenty years. If you will excuse me, I have matters of a very much living nature to attend to.'
He turns to the coachman, barking a few commands before stepping back into the coach. Already the tale of the foreigners who couldn't tell the living from the dead is spreading like wildfire in not-so-discreet mutterings. This is not what the captain had in mind when he bid you make the Empire proud.
120647:
Time has flown unheeded, and already the hour grows late. The tide waits for no man — nor, for that matter, do the ships’ officers. Your crew drain their last drinks then make their way slowly back to the harbour and the relative comfort of their berths.

When dawn breaks upon the sleeping city, the ship is already picking up speed, its sails taught with the promise of new journeys.
120649:
José casts a disappointed glance upon your crew.
‘I had hoped that seamen would be more adventurous. You would insult us by refusing bread and wine offered in the spirit of friendship? Or are you simply too close-minded?’ He scoffs. ‘You can find your own way out, I am sure.’
Before any of your crew can object, he swivels and disappears into the crowd.
Determined not to conclude the evening on so dispiriting an encounter, you head back to the tram and ride it through the city, back to the harbour through the most circuitous route available, enthusiastically remarking upon the wonders of the modern age between every clank and rumble of the car.
120650:
Your attempts at a Campanilese accent draw a few laughs from surrounding passengers, but the man's insistence on making broken conversation soon becomes trying for all.
One of your men mutters something about him minding his own bloody business — 'don't you have some goats to adopt?'
The native's face flares with fury, rounding on the sulking sailor and answering in your own tongue. 'I tried, but your Queen already has Sir Archibald.'
There is a stunned silence in the tramcar while your crew reel with shock and disgust, before a thick-set young lass leans in and knees him heavily in the midriff, sending him tumbling into a crowd of his outraged countrymen.
120652:
A roar of approval rises from your men as the man sinks to the floor, crimson-faced and groaning. Several burly moustachioed passengers leap into the fray, belts wrapped around their fists, only to be tripped and set upon viciously by sailors eager to vent weeks' worth of restlessness. A whistle sounds through the haze of torn upholstery - the local constabulary!
Your crew promptly jump down from the tram, with a flurry of jabs for good measure, and disperse into the surrounding streets.
120653:
A tram hardly makes for a convenient battle ground. Fists fly into errant faces, drawing bystanders into the brawl and ruining the plush new upholstery. When the coachman finally pulls abruptly on the brakes, sending everyone to the floor, the tramcar more closely resembles a dog-fighting pit than a coach.
Your crew scarper, dispersing through the streets with the shrill whistles of the constabulary hot on their tails. Some are dragged off for a night of holding, and the prospect of public disgrace in the morning.
120654: This is a fight we cannot hope to win
120655:
A wise person chooses their fights carefully — and a sailor, expected to report to duty on the morrow, wounded or not, doubly so.
Your crew hastily disembark from the tramcar, stumbling onto the street, and march back to their fallen comrade, ignoring the jeers and heckling of passengers roused by their aggressor’s anger.
The walk back to the ship seems interminable, and though all agree to turn in for an early night, the gloom of the abandoned festivities hangs heavy in your crew’s heart until the late hours of the night.
120657:
The Empire, eh? It is fortunate you have come on this day, for we are not by nature a forgiving people, and there is much history between us — most of it written in blood. But let us speak no more of this: tonight, we feast and revel; tonight we look to the future! See how swiftly the world changes — why, not a decade ago who would have imagined a tram here? Aye, in years past we drew blood, but tonight we draw wine, and drink to hope, and progress! What say you, por Deus?'
His hearty enthusiasm appears genuine, but you cannot help but wonder how deeply these past grievances are truly buried.
120658: ‘Let the strife of our parents die with them, then. To your good health!'
120659:
A beaming smile lights up his face.
‘Otimo! To a better world, and the bittersweet promise of peace. Let not our forebears cast long shadows over us — to peace!’
He seems to come upon a sudden idea. ‘My name is Alexio, and you must dine with me tonight! We have prepared food aplenty — the finest fare and freshest fish in the entire city, upon my word! Surely you will join us? Such a feast is best shared, and you would be most welcome! It is not every day our city gets its first tram!’
120661:
Alexio takes your eager crew through the streets of Olispo, skilfully weaving in and out of bustling crowds. Torches dance on the azulejos, a strange hypnotic flickering that makes the houses and high walls seem alive with warm, gay colours.
Everywhere, the sounds of chattering laughter, glasses clinking and food being shared fills the air.
A low-hanging door opens onto a bustling taberna — ‘Alexio, at last! We feared the port would run out before you arrived!’
Good cheer lasts well into the night, and dawn finds your crew rich with bonds newly tempered by joyous drinking, and the promise of a brighter future.
120662: Not tonight, friend. The first mate's very particular about early rising'
120663:
Obviously crestfallen, but determined to be amicable, Alexio helps the crew navigate a path through the crowds back to the harbour before taking his leave with a wave of his hand. He soon melts back into the throng.
As the last of the crew fall asleep in their berths, they can still hear the din of celebration in the distance, extending well into the small hours of the night.
120664: War is the province of kings, and we will not be pawns in their games'
120665:
He scowls, angrily. ‘What do you know of war, of sacrifice and duty? Many of my kin perished in what you call a game, for what they believed was right.’ His raised voice draws the attention of other patrons, their faces souring as they understand the tenor of the argument. ‘A man's land is his blood, the word of his king his command. I pity you that you cannot understand that.'
He spits contemptuously at your feet, then vanishes into the throng before any retribution can be exacted.
The silence left in his wake is ominous with untold resentment. You try to order a round of port, but the inkeep stares you out of the door.
120666: Only when Olispo has answered for its crimes will we have peace.'
120667:
He bows his head grimly. ‘Foul are the tides of war, and gore-hungry its hounds — none who spill blood can lay claim to righteousness. There are horrors in the past of both our nations. Yet is it not for we who follow to strive to be better? If we can, you and I, have a civil conversation, then perhaps there is still hope for friendship in our nations?
Vamos, let us extend Olispo's hospitality to you, and meet today as brothers rather than foes. To modernity, and peace!’
120668: A noble offer, and one we are glad to accept!
120669:
Alexio takes your eager crew through the streets of Olispo, skilfully weaving in and out of the bustling crowds. Torches and gaslights dance on the azulejos, a strange hypnotic flickering that makes the houses and high walls seem alive with warm, gay colours.
Everywhere, the sound of chattering laughter, glasses clinking against each other and food being shared fills the air.
A low-hanging door opens onto a bustling taberna – ‘Alexio, at last! We feared the port would run out before you arrived!’
Good cheer lasts well into the night, and dawn finds your crew rich with bonds newly tempered by joyous drinking and the promise of a brighter future.
120670: Not tonight, friend; duty calls, and rest
120671:
Obviously crestfallen, but determined to be amicable, Alexio helps the crew navigate a path through the crowds back to the harbour before taking his leave with a wave of his hand. He soon melts back into the throng.
As the last of the crew fall asleep in their berths, they can still hear the din of celebration in the distance, extending well into the small hours of the night.
120681: Alone in the darkness, they cannot hear her cries. Deep beneath this pleasant island of lavender and thyme she has fallen, to a musty, airless pit. She gathers herself and remembers the few safety matches left in her pack. You are her, she is you. Lighting a match, you are dumbstruck by a many-frescoed room, venerable and forgotten. A woman with a bull is the centrepiece— the great beast seems so vulnerable under her caress. The outline of a majestic horned door faces north, while a more humble passage heads southward.
120683:
In the next chamber, you find a set of stone shelves with fragments of wooden figures upon them — men, horses and bulls. Toys, perhaps? A distant growl rumbles across the walls, stirring dust from a pale fresco.

Facing east, a swan door. Facing north, flocks of herons make up a labyrinthine mosaic surrounding a pillared arch.
120685:
In here the ceiling feels lower still. Chipped tiles on the floor hint at a faded scene: a man, youngish and lithe, leaping over a flaring bull.
You lean in for a closer look, and notice all the tiles in the room are adorned with bulls' heads.
120687:
A dry click, then stillness. You shuffle over the tiles worriedly, letting out a low sigh when the last bull's head is cleared.
A narrow stairwell leads down into the dark to the east, while an uneven set of steps heads down to a wide passage to the west.
The fresco depicts a young woman passing a ball of thread to a young man. The depths grumble and growl eerily.
120689: A gaping chasm stares up at you where the floor has collapsed into a distant cave far below. A smoke-tarred beam, narrow and aged, stretches over the pit to the other side.
120690: Keep your back straight, and swiftly cross the beam
120691: A fine tightrope show, very deft! You pirouette to a halt, smile, and bow to no-one before taking in your surroundings.The ledge is small, facing a closed door. Chestnut wood, half-faded, supports an alarmingly life-like carving of a bull's head. Meanwhile, a cavernous rumbling — or is it growling? — seeps in from behind the door.
120693: Darkness there, and nothing more. Footsteps echo against a distant vaulted ceiling. You reach for a light and find one match left. One match — and then darkness.
120695: You tread a precautious path across the room, hands outstretched, fumbling for an exit. Something cold grazes your hand, then a moist, warm breath slowly exhaled. You feel a pronged spur jutting into the palm of your extended hand.A growling, thunderous and ominous, surges into your ears and face.
120697:
A great bovine head, cruel-pronged, flares into life as you strike the match. You let out a squeal, then something catches your eye: moss, growing on the creature's eye.A statue! Lifelike to a fault and of the finest craftsmanship, you discover that the brackish warm air, gushing in from a hidden aperture in the wall on which it is set, is being amplified ingeniously by the marmoreal beast's mouth.
A momentous discovery! An entire civilization, a hidden culture, a forsaken sanctuary... An epic for the ages! Thrilled, you reach behind the creature's neck to a glimmer of light, and pry open the brittle wall behind it to emerge into the fresh air of day.
120699: A monster! You turn heel and peel off into the dark, but everywhere you run walls and crossroads loom to meet you, and more than once you painfully collide with sharp angles or trip over unseen debris. Time fades, as does your breath. From somewhere far away, you hear the familiar whipping of sails — painted black, perhaps — let loose as the crew turn the ship to sea, believing you lost. Your head starts to spin. As you fall, a pale skeletal arm slides in and out of focus, as you wonder how many other sailor lasses have met their end here.
120701:
A dusty ochre light reveals a wide room with ornate-frescoed walls, the most striking of which is a contest between a hero and beast, half-man, half-bull.
Your eyes widen. A sudden growl surges into a roar behind you — you swivel to face it, but a powerful breath smothers the feeble flame at your fingertip. You have just enough time to distinguish the flared nostrils and sharp horns of a colossal bull before the darkness swallows you.
120703: You hold your breath, not daring to make a sound.Silence seeps through the shadows. After an eternity, you dare to stretch out your hand and feel for the beast. Your fingers find cold stone, tracing a jawline, then an eye... A statue! 120706:
You start across the beam, pacing a few painful feet before it creaks and sags downward. The surprise throws you off, and you fall into the pit.
You get up painfully, battered and bruised but very much alive. You light a match — one of few remaining — and find yourself facing a strangely ornate door. Chestnut wood, half-faded, supports an alarmingly life-like carving of a bull's head. A cavernous rumbling — or is it growling? — seeps in from behind the door.
120707: Crouch and crawl along the beam
120708: Trembling, you get down your knees and edge forward onto the beam, feeling its every creak and whine. It is slow progress, and more than once you cling to the beam as you feel it threaten to give way, but ultimately you come to a narrow platform facing a tall door. Chestnut wood, half-faded, supports an alarmingly life-like carving of a bull's head. A cavernous rumbling — or is it growling? — seeps in from behind the door.
120709: You kneel down on the edge of the beam and crawl painfully across its dark, narrow surface. There is the slightest of creaks before the beam gives way, rotten and broken by ages, and you fall into the darkness. The tumble is shorter than expected however, and you promptly find yourself — bloodied and bruised, but alive — facing a tall door. Chestnut wood, half-faded, supports an alarmingly life-like carving of a bull's head. A cavernous rumbling — or is it growling? — seeps in from behind the door.
120711: You come to a long room studded with husky alcoves, seemingly empty but for Ariadnean cobwebs. A rumbling sound startles you out of your observation — a storm, perhaps? Or.... Dust piles onto your hair from above, followed by several small but sharp fragments of rock, dully painted — the ceiling is coming down!
120713: You leap forward with the force of youth and desperation, darting through the increasingly heavy falling rubble before a final roll brings you to safety, as a fragment of rock larger than your head crashes onto the ground just behind you. Letting out a long breath you look around, striking one of your few remaining matches. A tall door graces the wall in front of you. Chestnut wood, half-faded, supports an eerily life-like carving of a bull's head. A cavernous rumbling — or is it growling? — seeps in from behind the panes.
120714:
You dash forward, but inhale some of the chalky dust stirred by the fall of the rubble. You stumble, a burning fit of coughing rising in your throat.
An ominous crack sounds right above you as parts of the coloured panes overhead shatter and come crashing down.
There is a blinding flash of light, followed by darkness, and then... nothing. Your companions will doubtless raise their black sails in solemn remembrance before journeying on without you.
120716: You wisely turn back as increasingly larger fragments of painted stone start tumbling from the ceiling with shattering cracks. When you reach the previous room, it becomes evident that most of the path ahead has caved in. With no desire to return to the ship just yet, you cautiously make for the second staircase you'd noticed. A short descent brings you to what must have once been a chamber. A dark pit stretches out where most of the floor has crumbled away. A narrow, precarious beam, is thrown across the chasm, a lone relic of once-complex supporting woodwork.
120717: You take a few tentative steps across the antique tiles, as an aching worry stabs at your heart — and rightly so, as it turns out, for you are only a few steps in when a series of adjacent tiles shatter audibly below you. You feel your feet swept away as a gaping pit rushes up to swallow you.
120718: Cling to the edge of the pit
120719: You lurch forward and grab one of the edges, pulling yourself up and out of immediate peril with a final leap towards the end of the room. As the tremors ebb away and the dust settles, you look around.A narrow stairwell leads down into the dark to the east, while an uneven set of steps heads down to a wide passage to the west.The depths grumble and growl eerily.
120720: You leap for the edge, but your hand closes on a sharp piece of debris. You cry out in pain, but it's too late. The abyss rises up to meet you. Harsh dust clings to your eyelids and burns your eyes as you plummet to the floor, where with a tremendous crack, you feel your bones shatter and the darkness take you. Your companions will doubtless raise their black sails in solemn remembrance before journeying on without you.
120721: Brace and prepare for the fall
120722: You brace for impact, knees bent and body supple, preparing to break your fall the way the other riggers taught you when you first joined the ship. It is fortunately no more than a dozen feet before you feel the hard ground below you send you immediately into a roll. Blistering pain surges through your ankle, but you're confident it's just sprained, and not broken. Trying to silence the pounding of your heart in your ears, you carefully climb the rubble back to the room, where two staircases await.
120723: You scramble to hold on to something, but everything is giving way around you. You scream helplessly, but to no avail — you are far too deep below the bleached hillsides, and far too removed from your fellow crew members for anyone to hear. You grab a jutting rock, but it gives way. As the darkness takes you, you feel yourself hurtle towards something far below — something only your broken body will ever know. Your companions will doubtless raise their black sails in solemn remembrance before journeying on without you.
120725: You leap over the tiles effortlessly and smirk at the figure in the fresco, challenging him to do better. You notice a second fresco, bolder and duskier, etched over two stairwells: one of them bears west, the other east. The fresco depicts a young woman passing a ball of thread to a young man. As you ponder your choices a deep, low rumble echoes from the depths.
120726: It's a poorly executed jump, as you slip on a loose tile. You feel a sharp pain in your arm as it strikes against a jutting rock, then the ground gives way entirely.
120728:
Mind-bogglingly complex mazes are etched in dark blue over every tile, on the walls, floor and ceiling. In the centre, a lone figure stands, minuscule amidst the labyrinthine landscape. The fresco in this room depicts a lame metalsmith.
Just then, you notice something cold lapping at your feet: water, briny and pale. It seems to be seeping in from a room not far off, facing west.
120730: An opening in the ground is slowly drawing in sludgy water from all parts. A fountain, perhaps? A ship dominates a large fresco on the wall — you wonder if it ever managed to return from its voyage unscathed. A large door with a familiar pattern opens to the south. You turn to face it when you notice a second, smaller door to the west. A soft hiss — the wind perhaps? — seems to be coming from it.
120732:
You push the broken door open. Something on the floor glistens not far off — reflected sunlight? You close the distance hurriedly before realising with horror that it was no light but a snake, long and sinister! All around you, its brethren slither curiously out of countless unseen nooks.
You take a terrified step backward and hear an angry hiss: you almost stepped on one.
120734:
It is dreadfully slow going, for the snakes curl lazily around your every footstep, intrigued as they sense the heat radiating from your body. Every step seems like an eternity, but at last you come to a short flight of steps leading up to some manner of dais, by which point the ophidians have been overcome with disinterest.
You dare to light a match, and something flickers in its shallow light: a statue of a woman, hand wrapped in serpents.
120736: A goddess, perhaps? Some long-forgotten serpent deity, left to sleep here untroubled? An ornate fresco stretches not far off, graven above two narrow stairwells leading east and west. The fresco depicts a young woman passing a ball of string to a young man. Grim, growling sounds echo from deep below, as you decide you must keep moving.
120738: There is something about the statue that makes your hair bristle with fear. You turn aside and look to the far end of the room. An ornate fresco stretches not far off, graven above two narrow stairwells leading east and west. The fresco depicts a young woman passing a young man a ball of thread, but as you draw near, a grim, growling sound echoes up from deep below.
120739: A more patient person might have navigated the serpent-weave successfully — or one with greater skill. When your match dies, a strange hiss overcomes the crowd of onlooking reptiles; you strike a new one up hurriedly. As the light flares back up, you make the mistake of letting out a relieved grunt, startling the closest ophidian! It rears its head angrily, baring long fangs!
120741:
You dart backwards with preternatural reflexes, narrowly avoiding the snake's lunges as it retreats into the shadows. Deciding you don't want to chance another attack, you bound across the room amidst the angry hissing, and come to a set of stairs, one facing east and one west, carved beneath an impressive fresco of a young woman passing a young man a ball of thread.
A low grumbling resonates far below, echoing in the stairwells.
120742: The snake latches onto your arms, fangs piercing flesh and drawing blood. You refrain from howling and instead grab it by the body, twisting its neck and throwing it among its brethren before bounding across the angry hiss of the room, cradling your arm. Two staircases lie ahead of you, facing each other beneath a vast fresco of a young woman passing a ball of thread to a young man.
120743: Crush it under heel before it attacks!
120744: The snakes flash forward, but you are ready: you dash aside and crush its head beneath your boot. A tang of blood and brine rises, and you feel the crowd of ophidians stir restlessly; not daring to wait for their reaction, you bound across the angry hiss of the room, reaching a raised dais beneath a pale fresco of a young woman passing a ball of thread to a young man. Two staircases, facing each other, forge a steep path into the darkness.
120745: You leap forward to crush the beast, but feel its fangs sink into your calves! You refrain from howling and instead grab it by the body, twisting its neck and throwing it among its brethren before bounding across the angry hiss of the room, as blood trickles down onto your foot. Two staircases lie ahead of you, facing each other beneath a vast fresco of a young woman passing a ball of thread to a young man.
120746: Stomp the ground with all your might
120747: You pound the ground with all the energy in your young limbs, hoping the vibrations will be enough to chase the brutes away. You hear a silkiness as many of them edge worriedly back into their hidden abodes. Suddenly, a movement by your ankle grabs your eye: one of the snakes means to attack you!
120748: A moment's hesitation — or was it fear — was enough for the irritated snake: it lunges at your thigh, latching onto it with long fangs.Gritting your teeth with pain, you tear it out, twisting its wiry neck before throwing the corpse towards a far wall. As its brethren slither towards it, intrigued, you slip across the room to a dais sporting twin staircases facing away from each other under a large fresco of a young woman passing a ball of thread to a young man.
120750: This place seems strangely familiar. The pillars, the tiles, the rubble... It's the place you first fell into this labyrinth, wherever it may be! Naught left to do but choose a new path.
120751: Return to the first room you found
120775:
Wide, sun-touched lands stretch out before you, long pale grass glittering with the night’s rain while a scattering of trees provides occasional shade from the already warm orange sun.
Unseen amongst the dense, matted grass, multitudinous creatures awake to the dawning day, nattering away gaily as the savannah comes to life.
A low dell not a mile away hides a blossoming waterhole, where numerous strange and foreign beasts are gathering before the day’s heat truly begins, nestled in the shadows of a set of monolithic spurs, looming high above the plains — surely with views worthy of a king!
120776: Scale the spurs for a bird’s eye view of the savannah
120777:
The climb is arduous and long, but your topmen trace a forgeable path for the other sailors, using thick ropes and residues of flour hastily brought over from the camp. At last, you reach the topmost spur — a long slab of ochre red stone, worn by countless rainfalls and storms.

Endless wildlands stretch below you, dust-coloured and windswept. In the distance, rainclouds swirl over a patch of darkness, and a deep golden hush falls over the land, broken only by the slow ambling of strange, tall-collared distant animals. A low threatening growl suddenly echoes behind you, and you turn to face lions, territorially baring their fangs at your crew. You have trespassed upon pride land.
120779:
One gunman shoulders his rifle and takes careful aim at a particularly large male, while the rest of your crew strive to stay as motionless as possible.
The shot echoes deafeningly against the surrounding boulders, and sends a threatening ripple over the lands below.
Cowed by the roar of the rifle and the sight of their pridemate slumping lifeless to the ground, the other lions slowly back away before turning tail and disappearing into the rocks overhead.
120780:
Whether owing to precipitousness or shoddy marksmanship, the shot misses the great creature by several feet.
Panicked, the would be hunter fumbles with the rifle’s lock, but an ominous crack signals the weapon’s reluctance to further use.
The lions take a slow step towards your huddled crew, hunger and wrath in their glare.
‘Someone hold them back!’ cries a sailor, before inching towards the first stone in the long series to climb back to the plains.
120781: Order your two strongest to intimidate the beasts
120782:
Two colossi, nicknamed Ajax and Hercules by your ship’s erudite skipper, step forward.
One of them roars a challenge to the assembled felines, startling them a few steps back into the shadow of the overhanging spur, while the rest of you swiftly start the descent.
As the last of your men slip over the ledge, a low, feral snarl is heard some way overhead. A host of lions have emerged from various crevices and alcoves around Ajax and Hercules — a pride of such size that there is nothing even a hundred men might do to fend them off.
A burst of raucous song comes over the ledge in Ajax’s baritone, and the very next second you see Hercules jump to meet you.'Run!' he says.
120783:
Two burly southerners, thick-necked and ruddy, step forward hesitantly while the rest of your crew slip as discreetly as possible over the ledge and onto the path back to the savannah.
There is a long-minute’s hushed, precipitous silence, before you hear whispers of quiet, nervous conversation up above, followed by an ear-shattering shriek.
One of the men topples over the ledge, plummeting to the distant grassland, as the other becomes the first of many harried by cruel claws and sharp fangs in a fraught and fearful descent.
120785:
Years of experience are easily forgotten in the face of mortal peril. Your sailors push and pull at each other to be first to descend onto the lower ledges, and away from the rampant cats.
One man stumbles and falls with a sickening crack onto the stone, blood soon clotting his hair and pooling on the dark red rock.
The smell of blood inflames the lions, and what reservations they had are forgotten, pouncing upon the stragglers, rending them to pieces. Pride's rock is a name whose irony will not be lost on your expedition.
120786: Throw the cabin boy to the lions
120787:
The captain knows he must do what is right. Do the lives of the many not outweigh the lives of the few — and are sturdy, aged hands not valued more in a storm than those of a youngling?
Yet the cabin boy’s wan, stricken face haunts him long after the garbled, bloodied crying — horrifyingly close, despite the distance — falls silent, at the claws of a merciful beast. None of your crew know untroubled sleep for many a week.
120788: Intimidate the beasts with loud noises and gestures
120789:
Acting as one, your crew start stamping the ground rhythmically, battering the stone with such force that it trembles while fiercely waving their arms in large circles, concealing their terror as best they can.
Startled, the lions slowly edge backwards, their low growls no longer threatening but worried, and promptly disband, gracefully bounding up among the stunted prickly bushes where their den must be hidden.
120790: Corner the den and smoke the beasts in
120791:
Dry wood and kindle abound despite recent rainfalls, and a series of short pyres are built around the lair’s entrance. Soon, bright flames cast deep shadows far back into the cave.
Rain-soaked grass and leaves are thrown onto the fires, spurting voluminous columns of creamy grey smoke.
There is a moment’s silence as the fumes invade the lair, before a powerful shape leaps through the haze — only to be caught by those lying in wait.
The lion roars its fury and anguish, to no avail, and your crew quickly return to camp, triumphantly bragging about their prize.
120792:
Finding kindle dry enough to start a fire proves difficult atop pride’s rock, especially with recent rains. You struggle to light small piles of damp grass and twigs, but your efforts only attract the lions’ attention. A female leaps toward a man struggling with a tinder box.
He ducks backward, narrowly avoiding a killing blow, only for blood to spurt to the ground as a ghastly tear appears in his jaw, his teeth visible through the wound. Your crew take cover behind what small, flickering torches they've managed to light, and start the achingly slow descent back to the plains, with their gored companion in tow.
120794:
Preferring to err on the side of safety, your captain orders a swift retreat down the spur, while the pride is cowed and cautious.
Evening finds you all huddled around the campfire, exaggeratedly recounting the encounter with the pride to those sailors who had stayed behind.
A sudden cry of wild dogs is heard distantly in the night, and you wonder at the beauty and majesty of this foreign land, strangely satisfied with the bloodlessness of your expedition.
120795: The pride is undeterred by your efforts to shout and stomp them away. Ignoring the increasingly high-pitched cries sallying from your crew, they prowl up to the edge of the overhanging slab, preparing to pounce. You look around at your crew, but the expedition up the spur seemed so harmless that none of them brought a rifle— save one lean and dark-faced young woman, who carries a narrow-barreled pistol model from overseas at her side. You feel entirely comfortable resting your odds of survival upon that. Cornering the lions when they land to subdue them might be easier, or repelling them with a hail of rocks?
120796: Prepare to corner them when they land
120797:
You order a loosening of the ranks — if the beasts pounce, they should immediately be surrounded —and not a moment too soon, as one particularly impressive male leaps into the fray. You prepare to corner it when a powerful fist crashes into the side of the beast’s head mid-leap, sending it sprawling, dazed, several feet away.
Surprised at the strength of Ajax, a surly but powerfully muscular gunman, your crew hastily retreat off the spur while the lion is stunned, and its companions cowed.
Tales abound around the campfire that night of the mighty feat of Ajax, without entirely making up for the crew’s sensation that they only narrowly escaped with their lives.
120798: One of the lions pounces upon a young man in the front ranks. He ducks, hoping to avoid the beast, but sharp claws rake into his shoulder, blood spurting violently as the lad crashes down under the creature’s weight. His companions pummel the lion with their fists, but it barely seems to acknowledge the blows, and busies itself with goring the unfortunate lad. All pretence of resistance finally abandons your crew; broken, the sailors disband and flee back to the savannah, routed and haunted by the dreadful fate of their young comrade.
120799: Order the woman to shoot, and hope that the gun works
120800:
Her face breaks into a dark grin as she draws the pistol to her hip with lightning speed. Sunlight glares off the silvery metal as rapid-fire shots flare from the muzzle with deadly precision and speed.
There is a moment's unbelieving, bated silence as four lions crumble to the dust, blood oozing from the small round wounds in their foreheads.
The woman smiles, satisfied, before returning her pistol to its holster with a flourish. A roar of whoops and cheers rises from your crew, and as they wend their way down from the spur, they crowd the sharpshooter to hear of her pistol — the last of the bolt six-shooters — and already, the legend of the woman who drew faster than her own shadow spreads like wildfire.
120801:
She draws the weapon with great haste, however, only one of the six rapid-fire shots hits its target. The lion roars, its mane matted by fast-flowing blood, while its companions furiously pounce on the young woman. Powerful jaws close with a sickening crack on her skull, bursting it open in a splatter of gore which sends surrounding sailors reeling and vomiting.
A famished growl is heard from above, before a newly woken group of slavering beasts jumps into the fray, rending with teeth and claw as your crew run for their lives.
120802: Throw a volley of stones at them
120803: You stoop hurriedly to grab a series of sharp rocks, pelting them towards the approaching creatures. They back away without breaking eye contact, clearly weathering the storm until there comes a chance to resume their hunt. Some issue low growls as the rocks hit their flanks, but most seem unworried.
120805: Much rather their stomachs be filled with this food than with you
120808:
Some of your crew weep to see vital supplies tossed to the beasts, but all agree that they would rather lose food than become food.
The offering pacifies the pride long enough for your sailors to head quickly back down the spur — a terrifying encounter, certainly, but one that is sure to reward them with many an admiring drink in the pub back home.
120809: You had expected to be back at camp by noon, and consequently brought very little food along — hardly enough to placate the hungering lions. Perhaps it is merely your imagination, but you think you hear a low rumbling run through the dark rock, as beasts from all corners draw threateningly closer.
120811:
Your party edges stealthily through the high grass towards the hidden waterhole. As they reach a ledge where soft soil has fallen into the muddy water below, they gasp in wonder at the teeming life gathered here. Scores of creatures huddle by the water — tall-necked giraffes spread their legs awkwardly to lean down and lap the surface, while nervous meerkats and contemptuous gnus eye the waters warily — and with the suspicious profile of those drifting logs, it's not without reason.
Suddenly, the ground shakes. You wheel about to see a manifestly infuriated rhinoceros charging at your company!
120813:
Your crew scatter as one tall woman, made lean by years of working in the rigging, steps up out of the grass to face the charging beast. She straightens proudly, defiance flashing in her eyes, and waits for the inevitable blow.
At the last instant, she steps gracefully aside, sending the beast hurtling into the thick tree behind her. Stunned by the impact, the rhinoceros staggers slightly, shaking its head to extricate its horn from the torn flesh of the tree.
120815:
Several sailors nimbly tie the creature’s legs together, carefully avoiding its thrashing head. The rhinoceros struggles against the binding, kicking out violently, but your men tug on the ropes and the beast comes crashing down on its side, motionless but fuming.
It takes considerable effort to drag it back to camp, but the dumbfounded look on the rest of the crew’s face is worth every bead of sweat.
120816: By the time ropes are brought out to secure it, the rhinoceros has already struggled free of the tree and rounds furiously at the oncoming sailors. They attempt as best they can to bind its legs, dancing dangerously in and out of a flurry of rearing and kicking, but the massive creature proves impossible to subdue, and it's not long before it surges out of the encirclement, thundering off into the savannah, much to your crew’s disappointment.
120818:
A horde of gnus stampede past your crew, evidently alarmed by the thunderous attack of the rhinoceros, separating you from the beast.
Leaping upon the opportunity to escape the maddened creature and its threatening bulk, you promptly retreat back to camp, thrilled by your escape — and the impressively dramatic skills of the woman who deceived the rhinoceros.
120819:
Your captain singles out a sailor renowned for manoeuvring rigging in heavy storms, and orders him to lure the beast into a nearby tree.
The man stands nervously, his terror evident as the rhinoceros bowls right into his path. He tries to lurch aside at the last minute, only to be skewered by the beast’s impressive nasal horn.
A terrified roar rises from the nearby waterhole as the gathered animals sense the gore and panic, their anxiety soon turning into a stampede! The few crew members that do escape the terror-stricken beasts will be forever traumatised.
120821:
Years of seamanship, climbing the rigging of a moving, storm-tossed ship, makes scaling low, twisted trees only a minor challenge.
The rhinoceros tromps to a halt when it realises its quarry has vanished, looking around with dull, rage-shot eyes before retreating into the sun-worn high grass.
As the sailors ease down from their hiding places, they dejectedly realise that the creature’s tonitruous charge has chased all the animals from the waterhole, and there is naught left to do but retreat back to camp.
120822:
The crew scramble for low branches and scalable knots in the thick, tortuous trunks of the surrounding trees. Most find easy purchase and disappear into the dense foliage, but a few are left attempting to scale a young silver-barked tree; supple and tall, but clearly unable to bear all their weight. They tussle for a foothold as the rumble of the rhinoceros’s charge grows nearer.
A third man attempts to hoist himself up, but his companions push him roughly, only to see the chap tumble into the beast's charge.
Satisfied that it has repelled its attackers, the animal leaves, but only after consciously trampling the body in full sight of every crew member, a scene that will haunt them until their dying days.
120824:
It is well known among naturalists that rhinoceroses have limited vision, and the information is quickly doled out to your crew in whispers. Taking great care to avoid sudden movements, all move out of the creature’s immediate path and adopt resolute stillness.
The beast grinds to a halt when it realises its foes have vanished. It tosses and turns its voluminous head, eyeing the high undergrowth for any sign of life.
After a long, breathy moment of indecision, it finally turns away and tromps down to the waterhole, to take in long, slow draughts of water.
120825:
Your attempts to convince the sailors to stay motionless would have been more efficient had four thousand pounds of armoured, horn-touting, furious beast not been hurtling towards them. One lad, seeing the beast drawing ever nearer, gives in to fear and breaks into a mad escape.
The rhinoceros immediately turns towards him, and your crew seize the opportunity to retreat, desperately trying to ignore the fact that in order to escape, the young man's life will be forfeit.
120828: Flee as far as you can
120829:
Attempts to outrun the rhinoceros are futile. Turning to the stragglers, it singles out a limping fellow and bellows, before charging and skewering him with its horn.
As the body of their crewmate is tossed and broken underfoot, your sailors flee back to camp, haunted by visions of a dark, bloodied horn piercing through the man’s abdomen in a spurt of gore.
120830: Encircle the beast to confuse it
120831: Rhinoceroses are swift, but their bulk lends them poor mobility. Your crew dance in and out of the beast’s vision, leaving it dizzily turning from one evanescent figure to the next. As soon as it is sufficiently dazed, your men dart behind the creature’s colossal backside and run hurriedly back to camp, hidden by tall grass, fearing at every instant they might hear a furious bellow, catch a glimpse of grey armour, or feel the sharp end of that osseous horn.
120833:
You order a loosening of the ranks — if the beasts pounce, they should immediately be surrounded —and not a moment too soon, as one particularly impressive male leaps into the fray. You prepare to corner it when a powerful fist crashes into the side of the beast’s head mid-leap, sending it sprawling, dazed, several feet away.
Surprised at the strength of Ajax, a surly but powerfully muscular gunman, your crew hastily retreat off the spur while the lion is stunned, and its companions cowed.
Tales abound around the campfire that night of the mighty feat of Ajax, without entirely making up for the crew’s sensation that they only narrowly escaped with their lives.
120834: One of the lions pounces upon a young man in the front ranks. He ducks, hoping to avoid the beast, but sharp claws rake into his shoulder, blood spurting violently as the lad crashes down under the creature’s weight. His companions pummel the lion with their fists, but it barely seems to acknowledge the blows, and busies itself with goring the unfortunate lad. All pretence of resistance finally abandons your crew; broken, the sailors disband and flee back to the savannah, routed and haunted by the dreadful fate of their young comrade.
120836:
Guns are nervously loaded and trained on the creatures, when a sudden burst of rapid-fire shots sallies from the rear ranks of your crew. Three of the lions stumble before falling at your feet, heads bloodied by uncannily precise sharpshooting.
The remaining lions back away in terror as your crew wisely head back down the spur, gushing proudly about the young shooter’s skills, yet unpleasantly aware of how narrowly they just avoided death.
120837:
Your crew fumble to load their weapons, and a volley of haphazard shots crackles through the warm air. Without the proper time to aim, the marksmen miss the beasts by several feet.
Enraged, the lions pounce, ripping and goring those nearby with powerful maws, spattering blood through the air and onto the rest of your horrified party. Abandoning all pretence of bravery, they flee the towering rocks, followed by the dying cries of their comrades.
120842:
Tales abound of a city sacred to all in this land, and of the holy pilgrimage that must be undertaken by the faithful at least once in their lifetime. Intrigued, you dock at a busy port — a major hub for those on this journey.

As you wander the streets in the cooling shade of antique rushans, the dust-hemmed white robes and sturdy sandals of the passers-by betray their wearer’s devout intentions. Snippets of enthusiastic and fervent chatter convince your crew that they must see this holy city for themselves. You are perusing an eager trader’s wares when a man approaches, ornate weapons latched to his side and back.‘Marhaban, friends. Are you here on pilgrimage?’
120843: Aye, we come from afar to see the Holy City.'
120844:
He eyes you sympathetically.
‘The wadi is a dangerous place — rainfalls and b’adawi brigands abound. Join the caravan, it will be safer.’
Such a generous offer is hard to decline, and the following dawn finds you clad in the white garb of the devout, joining the steady pace of hundreds of other pilgrims along the long, dry riverbed. The journey is slow, but safe, and it is barely noon the next day when the caravan reaches the outskirts of the Holy City and slowly disbands.
You look around, uncertain where to head to next.
120845: Head for the temple to complete your pilgrimage
120846:
Crowds flock to a vast walled courtyard with intricately arched colonnades. Intrigued, you follow the throng, but find the yard is entirely empty save for a towering structure of gilded black stone at its centre.

Swept up in the procession, you cannot help but be awed by the drone of countless muttered, fervent prayers. The devout circle the stone in ever-nearing cycles, it being perhaps the most important part of their often months-long journey to this, the holiest of cities.

A man in priestly garb hails you from an alcove in the creamy stone walls, amicably pointing at a panelled door behind him. He seems friendly enough, but then you still have much to do before leaving the city.
120848:
Seizing the opportunity to leave the stifling crowd, you follow him into a set of dimly lit rooms smelling of frankincense and myrrh.
All around, walls are piled high with ancient-looking books and maps — tomes of venerable learning in a score of languages and scripts, a testament to the man’s profession as a scholar.
One book in particular sits nonchalantly on a small red velvet cushion below the wooden arabesques of a slender window, its thick leather cover finely inlaid with minute gems and golden ink.
120849: Ask where he learnt such an array of languages
120850:
‘A language is the heart of a people, its sound the music of the world they hear, its grammar the image of their understanding, its history another tale of creation.' He leans quietly on the back of a comfortable low chair, eyes lost in the haze undulating warmly outside the Moorish window.

‘A poem tells of how the birds once joined in pilgrimage to find the Simorgh; how he spoke to each in its language, and how they knew thence the Truth of his words.’ He smiles with such joy that the weariness of age fades from his face for a while. ‘Long have I idled here, lost in what I knew. It is time I learnt anew, and heard the songs of birds of all nations — if you would have me?’So wise a man could be a great blessing on your onward journey.
120852:
‘A work of faith and learning, compiled by many a scholar wiser than I. But I would warn you, friends, to divert your eye from the glint of opulence and riches so displayed. You'll find the beauty of the Almighty brighter in dust and misery, than in the golden halls and bindings of many a treasure.’
With a twinkle in his eye, he thanks your crew for their company and bids they take their leave so he may prepare for a conference of the learned in the evening.
120853: Treasure in dust, he said — perhaps the city?
120854: Treasure in dust, he said — the desert, surely?
120855: Comment upon the antiquity of some volumes
120856:
He reaches up to a high shelf and retrieves a book with script flowing across its cover.‘The Book of Kings. A history of many lands and peoples, lest we forget our roots.’ He then traces his finger to the endmost volume in the line, carefully bringing it out. ‘My own journal. All that I do, and all that I think is recorded here’. Last, he pulls a voluminous book from another shelf — frayed and worn by countless years of reading, he hands it to you reverently. ‘The holiest book of all, that you may learn and wonder.' His eyes twinkle. 'Some pages are worn white with time — perhaps newer hands are expected to write their own journeys therein?’
You thank him profusely, and he bids you, and the book, safe travels, in the light of the Holy City.
120857: Leave the city before the pilgrims flock out of the temple
120858:
Nowhere in the city can accommodation be found for a party such as yours, so you set up camp in the hillocks outside the walls. Some of the pilgrims and travellers seem to have had a similar idea, and it is not long before a lively community bids you join their midst for the night.
As the sun sinks below the hills, food aplenty arrives to break the fast. Some pilgrims take up odd, long-necked instruments, and sailors trill merry dances on their own tin whistles and fiddles, delighting the children of the camp.
Long does this chance meeting, under a twinkling wreath of stars, stay in your expedition's hearts.
120859: There is more to being a pilgrim than donning white robes. Your attempts at mingling with the crowd go unheeded at first, and you join the flocks of worshippers circling around what seems to be a large, intricately gilded black stone cube. The procession is painfully slow, however, and the searing sun soon makes your party thirsty. One of them spots a well in the corner of the esplanade and rushes to it, cupping his hand in the fresh, clear pool. A roar of indignation erupts from the surrounding pilgrims as they lunge at him for tainting the sacred water, sending a ripple of confusion across the crowds — people scatter and stumble, swiftly turning the incident into a stampede!
120860: Attempt to push through to the gates
120861:
So few cannot turn so overwhelming a tide, and your attempt backfires spectacularly when some of your party trip on the hems of their robes, sending them sprawling to the ground.
Their fellows spring up to assist them, but already it is too late: the relentless press of the crowd, mindless in its fervour, carries them away, their garbled cries soon cut short by the crush, and thousands of stampeding, deadly feet.
A series of carved walls looms close by; perhaps they could be used to escape — or perhaps it would be wiser to fall apace with the throng until the unrest settles.
120863:
You flatten yourselves against the wall, gripping the jutting edges of the carvings to resist the pull of the tide of pilgrims. Bodies press in from all sides, stifling an already thinning supply of air. One man collapses and is caught. As you attempt to haul him back up, a ripple goes through the crowd and he is thrown into a stone pillar.
You hear a crack as his head collides with a sharp edge, and he slumps to the floor, lifeless and out of reach.
You inch carefully along, clutching at etched verses, before reaching a low door which mercifully opens, letting you all tumble into the safety of a side garden. As you catch your breath, you cannot help but wonder if the tragedy would have occurred had you not trespassed on holy ground.
120864: Huddle together and give in to the flow
120865:
You abandon yourself to the flow of worshippers for what seems like an eternity. The drone of thousands upon thousands of prayers is deafening, and the glare of the sun on the sea of white robes dazzlingly blinding.
At last, the slow swirl of pilgrims relinquishes you to the great gates of the temple, spilling you out onto the streets amid a hush of passersby. With your foreign dress evident through the tears and dark stains of your robes, you decide not to risk incurring the further wrath of the forces which rule the Holy City, and commence a faltering, mournful journey on.
120866: Try to follow the flow of the crowd
120867:
Despite its erring press, the flow soon brings you near a secluded alcove. In a powerful surge of determination, some of your burlier sailors forge an ephemeral path through the throng, and your crew stumble into the hollow, piling on top of each other as the pressure from the crowd suddenly vanishes.

A cursory glance around reveals a low, scalable wall, and you soon find yourself back in the less crowded avenues of the city, your lack of injury nothing short of a miracle.
120868: Respect the pilgrim's faith and head for the souq instead
120869:
The dust-swathed souq is vibrant and crowded with oddities, which both satisfy your party’s curiosity and lighten their purses. Most seem glad of your decision to forego completing the pilgrimage, though the more adventurous are tantalised by it.
Wearied by the heat of the day, you find a shaded, minareted garden and recline to watch the sun set on the city’s gleaming spires, idly toying with your new-found wealth of souvenirs — each a memory of a decidedly unique experience.
120870:
Perhaps he would have believed you were it not for the ostentatiously heathen jewellery sported by some of your crew. 123816:
A Day in the Life of a Priest


The priests of Kidusi follow strict rules and rituals on every god-given day.

DUTIES

Morning: ablutions.

Noon: ablutions.

Evening: ablutions.

Rituals

All ablutions to be performed in the Holy Pool.
Time between ablutions can be spent in the village.
Labour and crafting are prohibited.
Only the followers of the True Faith of Enbesa may live within the community.
Only ordained priests can wear the traditional tattoo of Kidusi on their face and wrist. New recruits shall show their naked wrist to prove their identity.


So were the rules laid out after the dark rule of Sûrya, whose flames devoured all books on Kidusi. Cursed be his name.
123817:
The Foundation of Enbesa


And as they rode the waves, seeking the Promised Land, the Queen bid the gods calm the raging storm.

And so the Gods did comply, and the waves rose higher than mountains on either side of the ship, yet the waters before us were becalmed and clear, and ahead lay the golden plain of Enbesa.

So the Queen did lead her people through the sea, where leviathans roam, and build a mighty city there — and in that city, she raised a temple to her lost husband Selamawi, and those who had stayed with him in Sile'Amidos, beyond the confines of the world.

Treastise on Heresy in the Golden Age


(...)

Heresy is that which the powerful would not see survive in their dominion. In the Golden Age, Sûrya burnt down the whole of Enbesa, his very country, in a rage of madness.
He branded the Kidusi outlaws and heretics, and tortured anyone who would not renounce the True Faith. Many died.

(...)

But the true meaning of heresy is a lie to the soul. And any physical representation of divinity can only be a lie, as divinity transcends what the servants can see. Thus, idolatry is heresy.

123820:
On Troglodyte Architecture


The tradition of carving homes into the very rock of the mountain seems to have originated in Sile'Amidos, but the people of Enbesa gave up on this architecture as soon as they settled in the Promised Land, for mountains were scarce.

Following the depredations of the Sun King Sûrya on Kidusi, however, and the burning of the Library and all it contained and of many priests' homes, Kidusi Anitoni resumed the practice of rock-dwelling, building their temple within the living rock of the island, so that it should be indestructible.

This happened right after Sûrya's reign, under the Age of the Princes.
123821:
The Ogdoad of Virtues


Eight senses: touch, sight, taste, smell, hearing, wisdom, emotion, instinct.

If something expresses itself through each of them, then it must be divine, as nothing can access human senses better than divinity.

Senses are our way of feeling and understanding the divine, and as such, training each of them is a virtue; training but one is for naught.

(Last page of the diary of Mekdem's Guard)

(...)

No matter how long I stay, no matter how at home the locals make me feel, there is always a shadow — a flame over my shoulder. Somewhere inside, a part of me is still running, escaping the bloodshed of Angereb. Tomas' rampage, the blades in my King's chest as he stood his ground to let his wife and son flee...

I failed him, so I could protect little Haile. But all I could do was leave the boy to run off into the city streets — my king's son, almost my own son, gone. Left to bear the terrible burden of his blood and trauma alone...

I wish, sometimes, we had never left the palace nursery, and found a way to hide there instead. It was such a quiet, peaceful place. A place of happier times, and wooden toy soldiers. Haile loved them so.

May you find solace, my young king, in this life or the next. Until we meet again. Not long now...

Copy the original text, then throw it in the well. Perhaps, one day, that truth will be every bit as needed as its destruction is today, when we have all been long returned to dust. But that time is not now.

130498: Ketema wishes to discuss the future of Waha Desher with you.
130500: Ketema rejoices to hear that water has returned to Waha Desher. He now wishes to discuss his further plans for the island.
130502: Tell me then: why should I squander any more of the resources I need to expand my empire, just so these islanders can feast and waste their days away? It is time for such irresponsibility to change. If Enbesa is to thrive and become great, all must play their part, even Waha Desher. I will not have them merely survive. They must grow prosperous and contribute to the nation's efforts — or be left behind.
130505: There is land aplenty here, enough to feed the entire Empire! These old stones must be torn down, and water returned to the drylands. No longer will theirs be a language arcane to all — the time for industrious rejuvenation has come for the oasis.
130506: This would destroy Waha Desher's unique identity!
130507: That is the point. You think their manners quaint and amusing, but they are foreign and antiquated. There is no place for an alien culture in a united Enbesan Empire. In restoring the oasis and farmland, we will lift them out of poverty and make true Enbesans out of them.
130508: My men will be ready to start as soon as they are needed. In the meantime, I ask you to tear down those forsaken piles of stone. We will need as much ground as we can to carve the deep canals and prepare the farmland.
130509: I will not be a part of this act of vandalism!
130511: Then let them be your burden! I will not bleed the Enbesan stockpiles any further for these ingrates and layabouts! If you so wish to keep this piece of mummified history alive, then let it be on your shoulders to not let them suffocate amidst the dust and rags of their dead land!
130513: It is no pleasant duty, but such are also the burdens of an Emperor. We must look to the greater good. History will remember the well-builders and unity-weavers, not the dust-and-ruins hoarders. And so we must settle our consciences with the guilt, that all may thank us for the prosperity this sacrifice will bring.

130521:
There is much to be done that the chieftain would gladly discuss with you, but once concern is greatest of all: ensuring that the Emperor's decision to forsake Waha Desher will not cripple the island's population and their livelihoods. A dismal fate it would be to see these shores forsaken; its lands abandoned to the shifting slither of snakes and the dull hoof-beats of masterless beasts.
If this grim prophecy is to be avoided, there is but one solution: you must provide Waha Desher with a new delivery as soon as possible!

130954:
ENBESAN CHRONICLES



Long before Enbesa existed, its people lived in the blessed realm of Sile'Amidos, where God had laid his head to rest after Creation. There bloomed flowers more beautiful and fragrant than anywhere else in the land, which the people grew and gathered for the glory of the Creator.

But after an age of prosperity comes a time of hardship. Cruel, dry winds swept over Sile'Amidos year after year, and slowly the land withered. So God sent a Covenant to King Davan, that great hanging gardens should be built to honour the sacred plants, and none would be sacrificed to the Heavens any longer.

The priest held the people to the Covenant, and all prospered again. The gardens saw the crimson flowers of immortality bloom anew, and became known as Deathless Grace by the many travelers who came from distant lands to trade.

But a time of Wrath came, when Sile'Amidos grew proud and haughty, and the Lord sent his vengeance upon them with water, fire and earth. Though the people bowed and prayed, the Covenant had been broken, and there was no mercy to be had. So Queen Shaba, the eldest of her line, took to the sea in great ships of dark wood, and with her went the farmers, the craftsmen, the priests and the holy women; and on her flagship, a chest of ebony, guarded by her son Elam the young, which held the broken Covenant.

130965:
Chapter I: The Golden Age
Was Eden just an illusion?



The shores where Queen Shaba’s exodus expedition landed were those of Taborime. The Queen ordered the construction of a new capital in the new-found land, as well as Elam’s Temple, to honour her husband who refused to leave Sile’Amidos. The Covenant — the symbol of the blessed dynasty of the Elamaïs — was placed within those new holy walls, and the Queen proclaimed her rule over Taborime. This is how Enbesa was founded.


Alongside her lost husband’s temple, Shaba erected her palace in the centre of Taborime. Built with the resistant materials of Sile’Amidos, its foundations are still standing today, and indeed are still used in the time of Ketema, Emperor of Enbesa.

The arid land was fertilized with canals, and seeds imported from the sunken island flourished once again: Sile’Amidos was restored, and the priests ordered the wise distribution of the holy goods. Under such conditions, the Enbesan population rose quickly, and Taborime's fertile lands became insufficient. This is when Queen Shaba contacted the neighbouring kingdom of Kashta, holding fertile oases to the West.
130966:
Taharqa the Wise, King of Kashta, agreed to bequeath the oases of Waha Desher to the young nation of Enbesa, in return for a pledge of unconditional help and support should Kashta require it. This pledge was inscribed in both Ancient Enbesan and Kashtan scripts on the Oathstone of Waha Desher, which stands to this day as a testament of the alliance.


Fearful of once again feeling the wrath of the Lord, the Enbesan high priests decreed all craft and tradesmanship impure, casting merchants and craftsmen out of Taborime and into the drylands of Angereb, to live in wretchedness and contempt, and never again see the luminous wreaths of the sacred plants. And so did Angereb fester rather than rise, bearing in their hearts the burden of a paradise lost, and unity forever broken.


Kashtan influence grew in Enbesa, much to the displeasure of the priests of Waha Desher. In time, dissenters fled into the highlands and founded a new temple, which they called Kidusi Anitoni. Kidusi Anitoni was a place of hallowed contemplation, and yet is all but forgotten today, save for just one statue.

130978:
In the rugged dells of their new land, the priests sowed and grew the sacred Deathless Graces, which came to be known as Hibist-Kush as their fame spread even to remote Kashta.


Time spiralled on, and the King of Kashta aged and grew ill. He sent for the famed priests of Kidusi Anitoni, demanding the secret seeds of immortality preciously stored in their high granaries. The priests obliged, honouring the ancient Oathstone covenant — but alas, they were all deceived, for though the lore of Kidusi brought the King back from the gates of the underworld, his solemn gratitude hid his darker designs. He sent thieves to Kidusi, who broke into the temple at night to claim the flower of Eternity, before setting fire to the granaries and fields. Flames ravaged the narrow valleys, and from then on nothing more grew in Kidusi — nor did the King of Kashta suffer vengeance, for his power was great and fearsome. And so the priests of Kidusi turned to writing history, and built a new temple and library on the ruins of the granaries — even if, in turn, they came to forget their mission.


There soon came a time of tensions between Kashta and Enbesa, and in a time of darkness, Kashta broke the sacred oaths and sent mighty conquering chariots to Waha Desher, stealing the remaining sacred plants while burning and salting the fields. Fearing for his people, King Ezana the Pacifist, of Enbesa, yielded to the invaders, but his son, Sûrya, was full of wrath and vengeance. He murdered his father and seized the crown, declaring Enbesa's heritage in mortal peril and swearing unending war upon the invaders.

130982:
He broke the dissenters with fire and cruelty and, with the help of renewed trade with distant lands, raised a mighty host. Angereb was the first to fall, conquered in blood, before Sûrya came to Waha Desher in arms. Furious at their reverence of the Kashtan oracle, the King ordered the entire population flayed and burnt alive — but one of his generals, Esato, refused to spill any further Enbesan blood. On hearing of the insubordination, Sûrya declared Esato a traitor, and ordered him to be tortured — his broken body paraded through the streets of the ksar. So was the last dissenter silenced, and the Age of Darkness of Enbesa began.


Sûrya ruled unchallenged for many years, but the fear of assassination grew unchecked in him, so that he squandered much of the imperial treasury in fruitless quests for the mythical Deathless Graces, hoping to gain immortality. In desperation, he descended upon the halls of Kidusi with an incredible violence, believing them to be hiding the secret to the plants' location, and burned their ancient library to the ground when they could not comply. A grim mood soon came upon him, as all seemed lost, and upon the ruins of the library he began raising a cyclopean monument — a mausoleum that was destined to house the record of his glory for all eternity.
Alas, however, it was not to be completed, for Kashta's hordes saw Sûrya's weakness and assaulted the capital, pillaging it and stealing the Holy Covenant. Desperate, and believing himself exiled from the Lord's favour, Sûrya took his own life in an unknown place alongside his closest guard, and Enbesa became a Kashtan protectorate. And so the Golden Age of Enbesa drew to a close.
130983:
Chapter II: The Silver Age
The Age of Trade, Prosperity and Greed



The new Protectorate of Enbesa was granted to a Kashtan governor, Napata, son of Menepata, who took on the title of Lord of Enbesa. Napata was a renowned general, however, and had little interest in his new fiefdom, preferring instead to wage war on Kashta's foes on her distant westerly borders. After some deliberation, he entrusted the stewardship of Enbesa to Myrion, one of the first Enbesan nobleman to pledge loyalty to his rule.

Unfortunately, this soon proved to be unwise, for Myrion and his followers seized power during one of Napata's absences, slaying every member of the Kashtan Ochre Guard in Taborime, while inciting insurrections all across Enbesa. Within months, Enbesa was united again under one banner, while Kashtan troops waged distant, heedless wars.


Fearing the advent of a new, demented king in Sûrya's line, the insurgent nobles elected to share power in a seven-headed regency: one to hold Taborime, one for Kidusi Anitoni, one for Angereb, one for the Waha in Desher, and three to hold vast stretches of the land around Taborime. All matters of state were to be addressed in the newly built Court of Seven, in Taborime, and a proud monument was raised to the glory of the princes near the high walls of the city. So came the Rule of the Seven-Headed Lion.
130984:
Kashtan wars and Sûrya's mad quest had left Kidusi weak and battered, so that there soon came a time when the Seven decided to acquiesce to the priests' requests to be released from secular concerns. The ruling prince of Kidusi released them from their bondsmanship and retired to an island off Taborime, to rule and build there as he would, while Kidusi slowly turned to a new, fervently holy mission.

With the help of the Seven, a new library was raised atop the dark ruins of the previous one, where the priests busied themselves with collecting and compiling a new history — a true history of Enbesa's faith and legacy. A history that proclaimed the sacred character of their mission, forbidding holy men and women from manual labour, and erased any mention of the sacred seeds, for shame of having failed their duties. As keepers of memory, the priests enshrined their holy status and gathered writings and scrolls from all across Enbesa, securing their dominion over all matters of lore and law, so that none could ever challenge their authority again.

And so, many jealously guarded secrets, such as the Ancient Script, fell into oblivion, only secretly remembered in the deep halls of Kidusi Anitoni, and the memories of mystical holy men and women.
